Para que esta visión de cambio se materialice, se debe cumplir con la siguiente condicion clave: que las instituciones están fortalecidas y son modernas, eficientes, eficaces, transparentes y participativas, desde el nivel nacional hasta el local, garantizan el acceso a la justicia, seguridad y potencian la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia y centrada en las personas y sus derechos humanos.

oc.parentName: Crecimiento, desarrollo sostenible y resiliente con generación de trabajo decente
oc.name: Más personas, especialmente poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, mujeres y jóvenes, participan activamente y se benefician de una transformación económica y transición justa, inclusiva y sostenible, que prioriza la resiliencia climática, las soluciones basadas en la naturaleza y la protección de la diversidad natural y cultural de Panamá, al tiempo que promueve la diversificación económica, con enfoque de circularidad, que cree empleos y trabajo decente y reduce la contaminación y generación de desechos.
oc.description:
Teoría del cambio:
Para lograr este resultado, deben cumplirse al menos cinco condiciones clave:
Primero, se requiere invertir en capital humano mediante formación técnica, voluntariado y capacitación laboral, garantizando oportunidades para mujeres, jóvenes y otras poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, fortaleciendo la agricultura familiar y estimulando la transición de la economía informal al trabajo decente.
Segundo, todos los actores relevantes deben invertir en la gestión integral, equitativa, transparente y sostenible del capital natural, colocando el agua y la biodiversidad como bienes públicos estratégicos y promoviendo la conservación y restauración de ecosistemas.
Tercero, las instituciones deben formular e implementar políticas de desarrollo humano participativas e inclusivas que fortalezcan la productividad, el acceso a mercados y la innovación en sectores clave como la economía digital, las energías limpias, el turismo sostenible y la bioeconomía
Cuarto, es necesario adoptar prácticas sostenibles que generen capacidad adaptativa frente al cambio climático, la pérdida de biodiversidad, los desastres y la contaminación, promoviendo un crecimiento resiliente y regenerativo.
Y quinto, se deben promover inversiones alineadas con los Acuerdos Multilaterales Ambientales y marcos normativos que integren economía circular, infraestructura resiliente y gestión sostenible de recursos naturales, contemplando las necesidades de los más vulnerables con enfoque territorial.

oc.parentName: Servicios sociales básicos de calidad, equitativos, resilientes e inclusivos
oc.name: Para 2030, más personas, especialmente las que están en situación de vulnerabilidad, acceden a servicios sociales básicos de calidad, sostenibles, con pertinencia cultural y territorial, y con enfoque de género, que contribuyen a cerrar brechas estructurales y a garantizar el ejercicio pleno de sus derechos.
oc.description:
Teoría del cambio:
Para alcanzar este resultado, deben cumplirse tres condiciones clave:
Primero, más personas en situación de vulnerabilidad, incluyendo niñas, niños, adolescentes, mujeres, pueblos indígenas, afrodescendientes, personas con discapacidad, migrantes, refugiadas, solicitantes de la condición de refugiado, apátridas, personas mayores y LGBTIQ+, deben tener acceso a información sobre sus derechos, conocer los servicios disponibles y transformarse las normas sociales discriminatorias que dificultan ese acceso.

Segundo, las instituciones proveedoras de servicios sociales (salud, educación, protección, agua, cuidados, etc.) deben ser resilientes y fortalecidas, contar con personal capacitado y presupuesto suficiente, e implementar sistemas como registros únicos sensibles a poblaciones clave y nuevos instrumentos de medición que garanticen cobertura en zonas rurales, comarcas y albergues.

Tercero, se deben diseñar e implementar políticas públicas intersectoriales inclusivas acompañadas de mecanismos de coordinación, articulación institucional y planificación e inversión pública con enfoque territorial y de inclusión social.

oc.parentName: Buena gobernanza, participativa y eficiente, seguridad y fortalecimiento institucional, con enfoque de derechos
oc.name: Para 2030, Panamá contará con una gobernanza fortalecida, descentralizada, con instituciones más eficaces, accesibles a la población, interconectadas y con sistemas de información robustos, que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios públicos, incluyendo la justicia, y que contribuyan a la cohesión social y prevengan y reduzcan la violencia y la conflictividad, logrando sociedades y territorios seguros, pacíficos y resilientes a nivel nacional y local, donde todas las personas, especialmente mujeres y grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, gozan plenamente de sus derechos.
oc.description:
Teoría del cambio:
Para lograr este resultado, tres condiciones fundamentales deben estar presentes:
Primero, más personas, especialmente mujeres y grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad, deben conocer y ejercer plenamente sus derechos; participar activamente y de forma informada en los procesos de gobernanza, planificación y monitoreo de políticas públicas; acceder a servicios de calidad, incluyendo justicia, con enfoque de derechos; y contribuir al fortalecimiento institucional y la cohesión social.
Segundo, las instituciones deben ser fuertes, modernas, inclusivas y centradas en las personas, operando con eficiencia, transparencia y participación, garantizando el acceso a servicios, justicia y seguridad, y asignando recursos públicos de forma eficiente y equitativa, basándose en evidencia y en resultados.
Y tercero, debe consolidarse una gobernanza moderna mediante la actualización normativa, la digitalización e innovación, mejora de la infraestructura pública, fortalecimiento de capacidades, uso estratégico de datos, coordinación institucional efectiva y diseño de políticas públicas inclusivas y basadas en evidencia para construir territorios seguros, resilientes y cohesionados.

sp.name: People — According to the principles of ‘Leave No One Behind’ (LNOB), ensure that all human beings can fulfil their potential in dignity, equity, and equality in a healthy environment (SDGs 1–5)
sp.description: The achievement of SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDG/SDR 1 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 2 indicators prevalence of undernourishment and cereal yield have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 3 indicators maternal mortality rate, neonatal mortality rate, mortality rate, under-five mortality rate, incidence of tuberculosis, adolescent fertility rate, births attended by skilled health personnel, surviving infants who received two WHO-recommended vaccines, and subjective well-being have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 4 indicators net primary enrolment rate, lower secondary completion rate, and literacy rate have been achieved. No SDG/SDR 5 indicators have been reported in the data as achieved as of 2021.

sp.name: Planet — Protect the planet from degradation, including through sustainable consumption and production, sustainably manage its natural resources, and take urgent action on climate change (SDGs 6, 12–15)
sp.description: The SDG/SDR 6 indicators that face major challenges are freshwater withdrawal, anthropogenic wastewater that receives treatment, and scarce water consumption embodied in imports. The SDG/SDR 12 indicator that faces major challenges is electronic waste. The SDG/SDR 13 indicators that face major challenges are CO₂ emissions from fossil fuel combustion and cement production and CO₂ emissions embodied in imports. The SDG/SDR 14 indicators that face major challenges are mean area protected in marine sites important to biodiversity and Ocean Health Index. The SDG/SDR 15 indicators that face major challenges are mean area protected in terrestrial sites important to biodiversity and mean area protected in freshwater sites important to biodiversity.

sp.name: Prosperity — Ensure that all human beings can enjoy prosperous and fulfilling lives (SDGs 7–11)
sp.description: The SDG/SDR 7 indicators population with access to electricity and population with access to clean fuels and technology for cooking have been achieved. No SDG/SDR 8 indicators have been achieved as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicators population using the internet, mobile broadband subscriptions, Logistics Performance Index: quality of trade and transport-related infrastructure, and Times Higher Education Universities Ranking: average score of top 3 universities have been achieved. The achievement of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. No SDG/SDR 11 indicators have been achieved as of 2021 as per available data. No SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDGs 7 or 8 face major challenges as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicator that faces major challenges is expenditure on research and development. The assessment of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 11 indicator that faces major challenges is annual mean concentration of particulate matter of less than 2.5 microns in diameter.

sp.name: Peace, Partnership, and Other Cross-Cutting Issues — Foster peaceful, just, and inclusive societies and mobilize the means required for implementation (SDGs 16–17)
sp.description: The SDG/SDR 16 indicators homicides, property rights, and exports of major conventional weapons have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 17 indicator Corporate Tax Haven Score has been achieved. The SDG/SDR indicator that corresponds to SDG 16 that faces major challenges is Press Freedom Index. The SDG/SDR 17 indicator that faces major challenges is international concessional public finance, including official development assistance.

oc.parentName: Food Systems, Natural Resource Management and Climate Change
oc.name: People in Sierra Leone, especially the most vulnerable, are food and nutrition secure, benefit from effective natural resource management, are resilient to the effects of climate change, and equipped to prevent and respond to disasters.
oc.description: Under this first outcome, the UN will support agricultural production and productivity as well as availability and accessibility of diverse, safe, and nutritious food, especially for the most vulnerable population, and with particular attention to gender empowerment in the agricultural sector. In the event of severe climate risks, the UN will support integrated adaptation and mitigation measures, including strengthening disaster risk governance as well as sustainable management of natural resources.

oc.parentName: Human Capital, Essential Services and Employment
oc.name: People in Sierra Leone, particularly most vulnerable groups in rural and hard-to-reach areas, have equitable access to quality, gender-responsive essential and social protection services and decent job opportunities.
oc.description: The focus of this outcome is on strengthening the human capital base of the country, including the provision of quality health services as well as quality education and market-driven skills to provide gainful employment, especially for women and youth population, Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) and other vulnerable populations, that will contribute to the advancement of their human rights. Special emphasis will be placed on the provision of quality, gender responsive and inclusive essential and social protection services, including the provision of digital solutions and infrastructure, with the emphasis on Leaving No One Behind (LNOB).

oc.parentName: Governance and Economic Transformation
oc.name: People in Sierra Leone enjoy transparent and accountable governance systems and economic transformation that guarantee peace, rights, and social cohesion, particularly among youth, women, marginalized and vulnerable groups.
oc.description: This outcome is intended to support institutional strengthening and promoting an inclusive governance system for effective service delivery. Emphasis will be made to improve overall transparency and accountability in governance processes as well as promote rule of law, access to justice and human rights, especially for marginalized and vulnerable groups. In addition, efforts will be placed on improving economic diversification, by promoting the design and implementation of policies and strategies that create enabling conditions to harness the opportunities in the green, blue, and digital economy and promote economic transformation.

sp.name: TRANSPARENT, ACCOUNTABLE & INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE
sp.description:
STRATEGIC PRIORITY: TRANSPARENT, ACCOUNTABLE & INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE
Revised-National Development Strategy Priorities 
4.5.1. Political & Legitimate Governance
4.5.2. Economic Governance 
4.5.3. Public Sector Reform
8.6.1 Gender Mainstreaming and Women’s Empowerment
8.6.2. Youth Empowerment
8.6.4. Capacity Development
	
SDG Targets
5.5 Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life
16.1 Significantly reduce all forms of violence and related death rates everywhere 
16.2 End abuse, exploitation, trafficking and all forms of violence against and torture of children
16.3 Promote the rule of law at the national and international levels and ensure equal access to justice for all
16.6 Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels
17.1 Strengthen domestic resource mobilization, including through international support to developing countries, to improve domestic capacity for tax and other revenue collection 	

Agenda 2063 Goals
11: Democratic values, practices, universal principles of human rights, justice and the rule of law entrenched
12: Capable institutions and transformative leadership in place
13: Peace Security and Stability is preserved
17: Full Gender Equality in All Spheres of Life
18: Engaged and Empowered Youth and Children
Assumptions
	Peace agreement (R-ARCSS) holds and all stakeholders at regional, national, state and local level remain committed or can be persuaded to commit to the full range of peacebuilding interventions envisaged, including those national actors who are not currently signatories. 
	Improvements in governance performance (including reduction in corruption, increased civic participation and access to justice) builds trust and commitment to the peace process
	Government is committed to honour its existing (and expand) international and regional human rights obligations including those related to reporting and implementation of treaty body recommendations
	Civil & political rights are protected & promoted for all, including the media or marginalised groups, with a robust open civic space wherein Government stakeholders value and promote inputs from civil society
	Political leadership for removal of legal & institutional bottlenecks related to discrimination & exclusion
	Gender-responsive budgeting is embraced by the Ministry of Finance and key Sector Ministries
	Duty-bearers at all levels embrace the role of (disaggregated) data for development, in particular for targeted support to those left behind or at risk of being left behind
	The political leadership is unwavering in its commitment to full implementation of anti-corruption measures
Common Assumptions
	The UNSDCF guiding principles (LNOB, HRBA, GEWE, Resilience, Sustainability & Accountability) are upheld by implementing partners
	Identified priorities remain relevant to the GoSS throughout the programme cycle or changes can be incorporated in a timely manner
	Staff turnover in key Government positions is kept to a minimum to enable strong, effective working relationships between UN and Government partners, plus capacity development initiatives to translate into sustained institutional-level positive change
	Existing skills gaps and absorptive capacities can be measurably improved within the timeframe of the UNSDCF
	Financing for development can be leveraged and new partnerships created across public and private spheres to increase available funds.
	UN Agencies have the minimum financial, technical and human resources requirements year-by-year to implement the UNSDCF
Risks
	High #s of youth not in education, training or decent employment contribute to political and social instability
	Resistance of coalition parties to collaborate across all governance functions 
	Communal and politically motivated sub-national conflict creates access constraints
Common Risks
	Conflict in neighbouring countries spills over to South Sudan and disrupts UNSDCF implementation 
	ODA flows decrease as a result of a COVID-19 induced global economic downturn, concerns regarding persistently high levels of corruption or diversions to other fragile states/countries in conflict such as Ukraine
	Conflict among political parties undermines full implementation of the peace agreement

Participating UN Entities: IFAD; IOM; UNDP (co-lead); UNESCO; UNFPA; UN-HABITAT; UNHCR; UNICEF; UNMISS (co-lead); UNODC; UN Women; WFP

17: Full Gender Equality in All Spheres of Life

Assumptions
	Economic growth and the creation of training and employment opportunities builds trust and commitment to the peace process
	Political leadership for removal of legal & institutional bottlenecks related to discrimination & exclusion, including rights related to land, property and business ownership
	Barriers and discriminatory norms and practices that limit young women and men’s participation in the labour market are addressed.

	Government remains committed to a form of economic diversification which prioritises natural resource management and broader environmental sustainability concerns as well as job creation in particular for women, youth and other marginalised groups.
	The enabling environment can be sufficiently improved (including creation of appropriate national investment policies and strategies) to attract/facilitate investment flows, for expansion of industry, take-up of technology and innovation, growth of the green and blue economies
	Strong engagement, collaboration and interest from the private sector to invest in South Sudan and collaborate with the GOSS on development issues, using ethical practices which fully integrate sustainable development concerns, including human rights and protection of natural resources
Common Assumptions
	The UNSDCF guiding principles (LNOB, HRBA, GEWE, Resilience, Sustainability & Accountability) are upheld by implementing partners

	Existing skills gaps and absorptive capacities can be measurably improved within the timeframe of the UNSDCF
	Financing for development can be leveraged and new partnerships created across public and private spheres to increase available funds.

	Conflict in neighbouring countries increases cost of food imports, cuts short growth of cross-border trade and improved regional integration

	Persistent and increasing natural and/or climate change-induced disasters, including flooding and pest infestations negatively impact food production, food security and infrastructure development plans 
	Pandemics & epidemics halt or counterbalance economic and social development gains
	Inflation continues to rise, with food prices and cost of social services out of the reach of most
	Global demand for oil reduces as part of greener growth/renewable energy initiatives, resulting in lower revenue for GoSS
	Fluctuations in the global oil market undermine macro-economic stability 
Common Risks
	Conflict in neighbouring countries spills over to South Sudan and disrupts UNSDCF implementation 
	ODA flows decrease as a result of a COVID-19 induced global economic downturn, concerns regarding persistently high levels of corruption or diversions to other fragile states/countries in conflict such as Ukraine
	Conflict among political parties undermines full implementation of the peace agreement

Participating UN Entities: FAO (co-lead); IFAD; ILO; IOM; ITC; UNDP (co-lead); UNESCO; UNFPA; UN-HABITAT; UNHCR; UNIDO; UNOPS; UN Women; WFP; WHO (co-lead)

oc.parentName: Inclusive Social Well-Being
oc.name: By 2030, people in Eswatini are benefiting from efficient and resilient systems that deliver quality services, particularly for the vulnerable populations
oc.description:
Between 2026 - 2030, the UN system in Eswatini, in close relationship with the Government and stakeholders, aims to deliver transformative development results that address the country's most pressing socio-economic challenges.
This outcome area seeks to strengthen the efficiency and resilience of systems to deliver quality services, particularly for the most vulnerable populations. This includes women, youth, PWD, PLHIV, key populations, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and children. The result reflects a commitment to strengthening public service delivery systems that are inclusive, shock-responsive, and rights-based. It supports progress across multiple SDGs, including health (SDG 3), education (SDG 4), gender equality (SDG 5), reduced inequalities (SDG 10), climate action (SDG 13), and peace, justice, and strong institutions (SDG 16). Through this outcome, the UNCT will help build a more equitable and resilient Eswatini, where no one is left behind and development gains are protected against future shocks.

oc.parentName: Shared and Sustainable Prosperity
oc.name: By 2030, Eswatini has strengthened national systems that promote inclusive and sustainable economic growth and expanded livelihoods, especially for youth and vulnerable populations
oc.description:
In Outcome 2 of the CF 2026-2030, the UN in Eswatini aims to foster an enabling environment for economic development, empowerment and livelihood diversification, contributing directly to poverty eradication and inclusive economic growth. This outcome supports the Government’s efforts to reduce
poverty (SDG 1), end hunger and achieve food security (SDG 2), and promote decent work and sustained economic growth (SDG 8). The UNCT will work with national institutions, the private sector, and civil society to strengthen value chains, enhance access to finance particularly for MSMEs and promote skills development aligned with market needs. These efforts will help unlock economic opportunities for vulnerable populations, including women, youth, and rural communities, ensuring that economic growth is both inclusive and sustainable.

ou.description:
**Number of multistakeholder coordination mechanisms established and active**

This indicator measures the number of formal multistakeholder coordination mechanisms that have been established and are actively functioning to strengthen collaboration, information sharing, joint planning, and coordinated decision-making among relevant stakeholders. These mechanisms may include disaster risk reduction (DRR) platforms, emergency response committees, coordination forums, working groups, and other sectoral or inter-agency structures. The indicator assesses the extent to which such mechanisms are operational and contribute to effective preparedness, response, risk management, and coordinated action among government institutions, civil society, development partners, communities, and other relevant stakeholders.

oc.description: En 2026, la réalisation de l’effet 1 se matérialisera par des effets multiplicateurs de la croissance inclusive sur le relèvement des capacités de l’économie nationale pour plus de création d’emplois décents, des capacités de résilience économique du pays face aux chocs/crises, l’amélioration de l’efficacité des politiques publiques, l’accélération du processus de diversification de l’économie, le développement du secteur privé avec un accent particulier sur l’agriculture, une meilleure inclusion financière pour développer les PMI/PME et plus largement la modernisation du pays, conformément aux objectifs stratégiques de la Feuille de route gouvernementale 2020-2025.

oc.name: Thailand’s transformation into an inclusive economy based on green, resilient, low-carbon, sustainable development is accelerated.
oc.description:
The first strategic outcome that is being considered contributes to the NESDP priorities aiming at ‘Targeted Manufacturing and Service Sectors’ and ‘Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability’ to support climate action, biodiversity conservation and disaster management. To focus the UN’s support towards the attainment of this outcome, the UN will collaborate with the
Government and development partners to deliver on the following two focus areas, which contributes to ten of the milestones prioritized in the draft 13th plan: 
- Green growth 
- Resilient community/society

oc.parentName: Human capital development and digital transformation & inclusion as key enablers that will drive Thailand's transformation towards a more sustainable, innovative, inclusive and resilient future
oc.name: Human capital needed for social and inclusive development is improved through strengthening of institutions, partnerships and the empowerment of people.
oc.description:
The second strategic outcome for consideration contributes to the NESDP priorities enhancing Thailand’s human capital. The underlying premise is that people represent the true wealth of the nation. A healthy, well-educated and skilled population, evidenced through the high human development index and based on the foundation of being able to access and exercise human rights, is a good in itself. It will act as a catalyst that drives the transformation of Thailand. The enabling environment for such a transformation is also dependent on the ability of public institutions, systems and services to successfully frame and implement a coherent integrated policy framework, based on principles of equity, accountability, transparency and efficiency. To affect such a change and achieve the impact required, public services need to concentrate on measures that drive standards and outcomes upwards through a focus on quality improvement. To focus the UN’s support on the attainment of this outcome, the UN will collaborate with the Government and development partners including civil society, businesses and communities to prioritize two focus areas, which contribute to nine of the milestones prioritized in the draft 13th Plan. 
- Human capital development through enhancing access to quality of public services,
- Digital inclusion and transformation

oc.parentName: Promote socio-economic opportunity and equity for all citizens to create a more inclusive and prosperous society, where everyone has access to the resources and opportunities they need to achieve their full potential
oc.name: People living in Thailand, especially those at risk of being left furthest behind, are able to participate in and benefit from development, free from all forms of discrimination.
oc.description: The aspiration to leave no one behind is the touchstone of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Women and LGBTI people in particular lag behind their male counterparts across much of Thailand’s social, economic and political life. The energy and dynamism of young people will play a key role in catalysing Thailand’s enterprising culture in the post-COVID-19 landscape. Equally, older people should experience healthy and active aging, as Thailand is an ageing society. Ethnic populations and people living in rural and remote areas should have equal opportunity to those residing in urban areas. Evidence consistently shows the criminalization, stigma, discrimination and other human rights violations towards people infected and affected by HIV reduce service uptake and increase HIV infection. As already noted, the digital divide, nationality as well as status can hold populations back from benefitting and contributing towards Thailand’s collective development journey. In short, where barriers to inclusion and development exist, they need to be systematically dismantled and replaced with enabling opportunities and services.

ou.description:

ou.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Improving the legal and regulatory framework and reduction of barriers (geographical, financial, social) for access to quality social services 
▪	Improving the legal and regulatory framework, as well as specific policies related to the national child protection system strengthening
▪	Strengthening capacity for effective implementation of social assistance programmes among national and local organizations
▪	Strengthening the child protection governance structures, including coordination across government departments, between levels of decentralization and between formal and informal actors     
▪	Implementing structural changes in the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Population to roll out social protection services across the country, establishment of social protection directorates and departments in velayats and etraps. Expanding community-based social services and specialised services along with capacity building of social work specialists in each etrap.
▪	Strengthening the capacity of psychosocial support professionals and developing community-based services for young people 
▪	Strengthening rehabilitation centres under the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry as inclusive resource centres for cross-sectoral inclusive services for persons with disabilities (rehabilitation and habilitation, early intervention, inclusive education) in line with the ICF and CRPD. Promoting a multi-sectoral system of assistive technologies and products for people with disabilities as part of the national rehabilitation strategy 
▪	Introducing and expanding specialised support services for families with children, including reintegration services for families with children with disabilities and in difficult life situations 
▪	Increasing institutional capacity and improved referral systems and services to protect women and children from all forms of violence. Introducing a system of special services for child protection and prevention of child violence. Supporting systems to challenge social norms to achieve gender equality and eliminate all forms of gender-based violence 
▪	Strengthening a range of services and programmes available that prevent unnecessary separation from the family, including gatekeeping by competent authorities, awareness of the harms of institutionalisation of children, and family support services aimed at preventing separation
▪	Strengthening systems of reintegration support for returning migrants in vulnerable situations and their families through a case management approach across economic, social and psychological dimensions, taking into account their specific needs, vulnerability, age, gender as well as skills, knowledge and transnational networks they acquired in migration.
▪	Developing new social protection packages for different type disabilities (cash plus services) based on the additional costs associated with disability
▪	Strengthening inter-sectoral coordination and referral mechanisms to provide integrated services to vulnerable population groups

sp.name: Prosperity
sp.description: The UN focus under the prosperity priority is on increasing production, productivity and incomes, helping to accelerate the creation of decent formal sector jobs at the individual level. Additionally, it seeks structural transformation and higher levels of economic growth at the national level, a key focus of the Five-Year Development Plan 2021/22-2025/26 (FYDP III) and Zanzibar.

sp.name: Planet
sp.description: The third strategic priority is towards supporting a greener, more sustainable development path. This includes better access to clean energy and technology to fuel growth, enabling more sustainable management of Tanzania’s wealth of natural resources. It will also cultivate close partnerships with government and communities to mitigate against climate change and reduce disaster risks.

sp.name: Enabling Environment
sp.description: This strategic priority supports the realisation of the results across the other areas. The priority focus is on broader issues of representative and inclusive governance, accessing data, development planning and financing, access to justice, access to information, sustaining peace, and the expansion and mainstreaming of gender equality and human rights.

oc.parentName: Prosperity
oc.name: By 2027 People in the United Republic of Tanzania working in MSMEs and small-scale agriculture, especially the most vulnerable, achieve increased, more sustainable productivity and incomes with more equitable access to productive resources.
oc.description: The prosperity outcome contributes to the national FYDP III economic growth and infrastructure pillars, as well as the economic transformation pillar of ZADEP. The outcome is specifically aligned to the interventions for deepening industrialisation and service provision, together with investment and trade promotion in the FYDP III, particularly those related to agriculture, manufacturing, science technology and innovation, and the blue economy. The CCA shows that economic growth is primarily benefitting wealthier urban households. As a result of the UN system’s commitment to ensuring that no one is left behind, a key focus of this outcome is on ensuring that the majority of Tanzanians who are engaged and depend on smallholder agriculture and in MSMEs for their livelihoods – also benefit through increased incomes and productivity. These two activities contribute significantly to Tanzania’s objective to achieve upper middle-income economy status

oc.parentName: Planet
oc.name: By 2027, people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, contribute to and benefit from more inclusive and gender-responsive management of natural resources, climate change resilience, disaster risk reduction and increased use of efficient renewable energy.
oc.description: The third outcome of the UNSDCF contributes to the FYDP III interventions on inclusive development, environmental sustainability and climate change. It is aligned with the ZADEP pillars on governance and resilience, environment and climate change and safety, security and disaster management. The outcome seeks to ensure that “by 2027, people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable contribute to, and benefit from more inclusive and gender-responsive management of natural resources, climate change resilience, and increased use of efficient renewable energy”.

oc.parentName: Enabling Environment
oc.name: By 2027 people in the United Republic of Tanzania, especially the most vulnerable, participate in and benefit from government institutions and systems that promote peace and justice, are gender responsive, inclusive, accountable and representative, and are compliant with international human rights norms and standards.
oc.description: The enabling environment outcome is aligned to the interventions for human development in the FYDP III, where the focus is on good governance and rule of law, effective and efficient justice service delivery system, peace security and political stability. It contributes to the governance and resilience pillar of the ZADEP. Under this outcome the UN will work to support the renewal of the social contract and to support the closing of the gap between the people and the institutions that serve them as outlined in the Secretary General’s report on “Our Common Agenda.” Towards this, the UN will work on ensuring that “By 2027 the most vulnerable, participate in and benefit from government institutions and systems that promote peace and justice, are gender responsive, inclusive, accountable and representative, and are compliant with international human rights norms and standards”.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  1: HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
sp.description: This area aims to contribute to Mozambique’s priority to develop human capital and social justice. It encompasses addressing gaps in gender equality, people’s equitable access to health, nutritious food, WASH, quality education and learning, and social protection, particularly for women and youth, people with disabilities, people and communities in the most vulnerable and marginalized situations, including by addressing harmful practices and gender norms.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  2: ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS
sp.description: This area aims to contribute Mozambique’s priority to boost economic growth, productivity and job generation. It focuses on pursuing an accelerated shift towards more diversified, sustainable and inclusive economic growth, with increased and equitable opportunities for decent jobs and livelihoods and increased incomes, especially for women and youth, people with disabilities and displaced, the most vulnerable and marginalised.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  3: CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF NATURAL RESOURCES
sp.description: This area aims to contribute to Mozambique’s priority to strengthen sustainable management of natural resources and the environment. It focuses on accelerating actions on climate change mitigation and adaptation as well as disaster resilience. It prioritises improving the sustainable management of natural resources to enhance the resilience of infrastructure and human settlements and improve national productivity and GDP. It pays special attention to women and youth, people with disabilities, the most vulnerable and marginalised, and their rights to access information, participation and justice in environmental matters, as per Principle 10 of the Rio Declaration.

sp.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY AREA  4: PEACEBUILDING, HUMAN RIGHTS AND INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE
sp.description: This area aims to contribute to Mozambique’s priorities to strengthen democracy and national unity, promote good governance and decentralisation, and enhance international cooperation with special attention to women and youth, IDPs, people with disabilities, the most vulnerable and marginalised. It encompasses promoting peace and greater social cohesion through more inclusive, participatory and accountable governance and institutions for people to enjoy their human rights and access an equitable and fair justice system.

sp.name: Reforço do Talento Humano e do Capital Social / Strengthened Human Talent and Social Capital
sp.description:
Esta área estratégica prioritária visa contribuir para o objetivo de Cabo Verde de promover o desenvolvimento social através do capital humano, da inclusão e da erradicação da pobreza extrema. Incide sobre facilitar um maior acesso e utilização de serviços sociais essenciaismodernos e de proteção através do reforço de capacidades e sistemas nacionais, da capacitação dos titulares de direitos mais vulneráveis, e da melhoria das políticas publicas e regulamentação.

This strategic priority area aims to contribute to Cabo Verde’s goal of promoting social development through human capital, inclusion, and eradicating extreme poverty. It focuses on enabling better access and use of modern essential social services and protection through strengthening national capacities and systems, empowering the most vulnerable rights holders, and improving policy and regulatory frameworks.

sp.name: Transformação Económica Inclusiva, Prosperidade e Transição Justa para um Ambiente Saudável / Inclusive Economic Transformation, Prosperity, and Just Transition to a Healthy Environment
sp.description:
Esta área estratégica prioritária visa contribuir para os objetivos de Cabo Verde de assegurar a recuperação económica, o crescimento sustentável, e promover a diversificação, abordando ao mesmo tempo a sustentabilidade ambiental, a ação climática, e a agenda de resiliência. Prioriza uma transição para a economia azul e verde que cria empregos decentes para todos, assim como a segurança alimentar. Além disso, presta especialatenção às oportunidades de transformação digital e integração regional e global.

This strategic priority area aims to contribute to Cabo Verde’s goals to ensure economic recovery, sustainable growth, and promote diversification while at the same time addressing the environmental sustainability, climate action, and resilience agenda. It prioritizes a transition to the blue and green economy that creates decent jobs for all as well as food security. Furthermore, it pays special attention to the opportunities of digital transformation and regional and global integration.

sp.name: Governação Transformadora e Coesão Territorial Reforçada / Transformative Governance and Strengthened Territorial Cohesion
sp.description:
Esta área estratégica prioritária visa contribuir para o objetivo de Cabo Verde de maior coesão territorial, descentralização, consolidação da soberania nacional e governação democrática, e acesso adequado à justiça. Abrange o apoio ao país no cumprimento das suas obrigações em matéria de direitos humanos, maior responsabilização e capacidade de parceria para o desenvolvimento,
com um enfoque específico nas mulheres e na juventude. 

This strategic priority area aims to contribute to Cabo Verde’s objective of greater territorial cohesion, decentralization, consolidation of national sovereignty and democratic governance, and adequate access to justice. It encompasses supporting the country in meeting its human rights obligations, increased accountability and ability to partner for development, and specifically focuses on women and youth.

oc.parentName: Reforço do Talento Humano e do Capital Social / Strengthened Human Talent and Social Capital
oc.name: Efeito 1: Até 2027, mais pessoas, especialmente as que vivem em situações de mais vulnerabilidade ou marginalização e as que vivem com deficiências, terão acesso equitativo e utilização de serviços sociais essenciais e de proteção de alta qualidade, resilientes, sensíveis ao género e modernos. / Outcome 1: By 2027, more people, especially those living in the most vulnerable and marginalized situations and those living with disabilities, have equitable access to and use of high-quality, resilient, gender-responsive, and modern essential social services and protection.
oc.description:
Este Efeito é um compromisso específico da ONU em Cabo Verde para melhorar o acesso a serviços básicos e sociais de qualidade, dentro de uma abordagem de Não Deixar Ninguém Para Trás, reforçando os sistemas de educação, saúde e proteção social, através do desenvolvimento de capacidades institucionais e humanas e de programas piloto de prestação de serviços inovadores, melhorando a coordenação e o planeamento intersectorial e multinível. Está alinhado com os objetivos nacionais e globais (#ODS1, #ODS3, #ODS4, #ODS5, #ODS6.1-6, 6b e #ODS11.1, 11.3, 11.5, 11.a, 11.b e (#ODS3, #ODS4, #ODS6.1-6, 6b e #ODS11.1, 11.3, 11.5, 11.a, 11.b). Contribuirá também para o crescimento inclusivo (ODS8), redução das desigualdades (ODS10) e identidade legal (#ODS16). / 

This Outcome is a concrete commitment of the UN in Cabo Verde to improve access to quality basic and social services, within a Leave No One Behind approach, strengthening the education, health and social protection systems by building institutional and human capacities and piloting innovative service delivery programs and improving cross-sectoral and multilevel coordination and planning. It is in line with the national and global targets (#SDG1, #SDG3, #SDG4, #SDG5, #SDG6.1-6, 6b and #SDG11.1, 11.3, 11.5, 11.a, 11.b and (#SDG3, #SDG4, #SDG6.1-6, 6b and #SDG11.1, 11.3, 11.5, 11.a, 11.b). It will also contribute to inclusive growth (SDG 8), reduction of inequalities (#SDG10) and legal identity (#SDG16).

oc.parentName: Transformação Económica Inclusiva, Prosperidade e Transição Justa para um Ambiente Saudável / Inclusive Economic Transformation, Prosperity, and Just Transition to a Healthy Environment
oc.name: Efeito 2.1: Até 2027, uma economia mais sustentável, inclusiva, diversificada e integrada gerará empregos decentes, segurança alimentar e nutrição para os mais vulneráveis, especialmente as mulheres, os jovens e os mais pobres. / Outcome 2.1: By 2027, a more sustainable, inclusive, diversified and integrated economy generates decent jobs, food security and nutrition for the most vulnerable, especially women, youth and the extreme poor.
oc.description:
Através deste Efeito, o SNU pretende acompanhar a transformação económica (#ODS8.1-3, 8.5-9 e), apoiando uma maior igualdade de género (#ODS), coesão territorial, transição para a formalidade, inovação e industrialização em pequena escala (#ODS9.2, 9.3, 9.5, 9.b), com enfoque em empregos decentes nas economias azul, verde e digital. A promoção de mais transformações destina-se a alcançar a erradicação da pobreza (#ODS1.1, 1.2, 1.4; #ODS10.3, 10.4, 10.7, 10.b; #ODS17.15), diversificação económica, transição energética (#ODS7.1-3) e digitalização (#ODS17). Exigirá equipar as pessoas com as competências certas (#SDG4) e irá apoiar sistemas alimentares inclusivos e resilientes para melhorar a segurança alimentar e a nutrição (#ODS2), incluindo através da resolução de estrangulamentos críticos ligados ao nexo água-energia e economias de escala limitadas.

Through this outcome, the UN intends to accompany economic transformation (#SDG8.1-3, 8.5-9 and) by supporting better gender equality (#SDG5), territorial cohesion, transition to formality, innovation and small-scale industrialization (#SDG9.2, 9.3, 9.5, 9.b), with a focus on decent jobs in the blue, green and digital economies. Boosting further transformations are meant to achieve poverty eradication (#SDG1.1, 1.2, 1.4; #SDG10.3, 10.4, 10.7, 10.b; #SDG17.15), economic diversification, energetic transition (#SDG7.1-3) and digitalization (#SDG17). It will require equipping people with the right skills (#SDG4) and it will support inclusive and resilient food systems to improve food security and nutrition (#SDG2), including through addressing critical bottlenecks linked to the water-energy nexus and the limited economies of scale.

oc.parentName: Transformação Económica Inclusiva, Prosperidade e Transição Justa para um Ambiente Saudável / Inclusive Economic Transformation, Prosperity, and Just Transition to a Healthy Environment
oc.name: Efeito 2.2: Até 2027, os principais ecossistemas marinhos e terrestres e a biodiversidade estarão melhor protegidos, restaurados e geridos de forma mais sustentável, e a resiliência aos choques e impactos das alterações climáticas será melhorada e mais sensíveis às questões do género. / Outcome 2.2: By 2027, key marine and land ecosystems and biodiversity are better protected, restored, and more sustainably managed and the resilience to shocks and climate change are improved and gender responsive.
oc.description:
Este Efeito representa o compromisso do sistema do SNU de apoiar a adaptação do país às alterações climáticas (#ODS1.5; #ODS13.1-3, 13.b;) tendo em conta o género (#ODS5), apoiando o reforço dos quadros jurídicos, políticos e institucionais e as capacidades para proteção e restauração de ecossistemas marinhos (#ODS14. 2-5, 14.7, 14.a, 14.b), e terrestes (#ODS15.1-5, 15.9), redução do risco de desastres, gestão sustentável dos recursos naturais (#ODS6, #ODS12) e das cidades (#ODS11), e acesso ao financiamento climático (#ODS17).

This outcome represents the commitment of the UN system to support the country’s adaptation to climate change (#SDG1.5; #SDG13.1-3, 13.b;) while taking gender into account (#SDG5), by supporting the enhancement of the legal, policy and institutional frameworks and the capacities for marine (#SDG14.2-5, 14.7, 14.a, 14.b), and land (#SDG15.1-5, 15.9) ecosystems protection and restoration, disaster risk reduction, sustainable management of natural resources (#SDG6, #SDG12) and cities (#SDG11), and access to climate financing (#SDG17).

oc.parentName: Governação Transformadora e Coesão Territorial Reforçada / Transformative Governance and Strengthened Territorial Cohesion
oc.name: Efeito 3.1: Até 2027, mais pessoas, especialmente mulheres, jovens e grupos vulneráveis, exercerão livremente os seus direitos, participarão e beneficiarão de instituições inclusivas, resilientes, transparentes e responsáveis e de um sistema de governação democrática mais modernizado, transformador e eficaz que defenda o Estado de direito, a nível nacional e local. / Outcome 3: By 2027, more people, especially women, youth and those in vulnerable groups, freely exercise their rights, participate in, and benefit from, inclusive, resilient, transparent, and accountable institutions and a more modernized, transformative and effective system of democratic governance that upholds the rule of law, at national and local levels.
oc.description:
Este resultado visa apoiar a continuidade, mesmo num cenário de desenvolvimento adverso, da construção de resiliência e uma maior coesão (#ODS10), consolidando um dos principais trunfos do país para o desenvolvimento sustentável - instituições que funcionam bem e uma democracia sólida (#ODS16.1-5, 16.6-10, 16.a). Utilizando o seu poder de assembleia e as ferramentas criadas a nível nacional e global pelas Agências, Fundos e Programas das Nações Unidas, irá apoiar o financiamento destas transformações (#ODS17.1, 17.14), inclusivo através da emergência de uma forte coligação nacional sustentada por igualdade de género (#ODS5) e sólidas parcerias estratégicas, entre sectores e incluindo as autoridades locais, a sociedade civil, o setor privado e as universidades (#ODS17.17), bem como parceiros internacionais (#ODS17.3), parceiros de cooperação Sul-Sul (#ODS17.6) e PEID homólogos como prioridade máxima.

This outcome aims at supporting the continuity, even in an adverse development landscape, of resilience building and greater cohesion (#SDG10), by consolidating one the country’s main assets for sustainable development – well-functioning institutions, strong democracy (#SDG16.1-5, 16.6-10, 16.a). Using its convening power and the tools created at national and global levels by UN Agencies, Funds and Programmes, it will support the financing of these transformations (#SDG17.1, 17.14), including through the emergence of a strong national coalition underpinned by gender equality (#SDG5) and solid strategic partnerships, across sectors and including local authorities, civil society, the private sector and the academia (#SDG17.17), as well as international partners (#SDG17.3), south-south cooperation partners (#SDG17.6) and peer SIDS as a top priority.

ou.name: Output 3.1 Vulnerable and marginalized communities, including adolescents and young women, survivors of gender-based violence and harmful practices, youth, migrants, forcibly displaced individuals, the elderly, and people living with disabilities and HIV, have enhanced access to and participation in quality services encompassing education, health, HIV-AIDS, nutrition, WASH, sexual and reproductive health and rights, gender-based violence prevention and response, and social and child protection services, within the humanitarian-development-peace nexus.
ou.description:
Agency Name: World Health Organization
Key Achievements:
1) WHO technically and financially supported the monitoring and mentorship on Multi drug resistant Tuberculosis patient service delivery. The capacity built during the mentorship will benefit the 110 recent Multi drug resistant patients registered in Malawi. 

2) WHO financially supported expansion of PEN Plus services in the country, this will benefit over 6 million Malawians who have at least a Non-Communicable Disease.

3) WHO technically and financially supported training of 8 Clinicians in the management of rhodesiense Human African Trypanosomiasis (rHAT) using the new drug Fexinidazole. The skilled gained will benefit all rHAT Patients in Malawi since Clinicians were drawn from all the HAT districts of Nkhotakota, Ntchisi, Kasungu and Rumphi.

4) WHO supported MOH with 4018 filarial test strips for Post Elimination surveillance of Lymphatic Filariasis, 48 of the 4018 school going pupils tested positive and benefited from treatment.

Key Bottlenecks: Inadequate funding to implement all planned activities.
Lessons Learnt: 1) Any little support to the most vulnerable and marginalized population groups, makes a little difference.
                              2) It is important to link up for partnership support
Emerging Priorities: Need to amend policies and guidelines to include Gender, Equity and Human Rights so that no one is left behind from the planning stage to implementation.

oc.parentName: Inclusive Social Development & Well-Being
oc.name: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
oc.description: The outcome statement for SPA 1 centres on inclusive social development and well-being. This is defined by equitable access to quality social services and the realization of basic human capabilities, as outlined in the relevant SDGs and international human rights instruments. Key dimensions include education, health, social protection, and food and nutrition, with the aim of enabling all people living in Malaysia to realise their full human potentials.

oc.parentName: Economic Transformation for Inclusive and Sustainable Prosperity
oc.name: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
oc.description: The outcome statement for SPA 2 focuses on inclusive and sustainable economic transformation. It envisions a high-income economy that is future-ready, resilient and environmentally sustainable, driving broad-based growth and enabling opportunities for all, particularly, women, youth and populations in lagging regions. Economic transformation is approached not only in terms of growth maximization, but of structural change that enhances equity, sustainability and productivity in high value-added sectors focused on technology but also including high-value service industries (notably tourism). This includes diversifying the economy through innovation and digitalization by leveraging the Malaysia Digital initiatives to promote the growth of these digital industries, facilitating a green transition, helping to create decent jobs and more functional labour market and expanding economic participation and opportunity via targeted investments.

oc.parentName: Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
oc.name: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
oc.description: This outcome addresses the in-country impacts of the triple planetary crisis (climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution). It reflects growing vulnerabilities of Malaysia’s natural environment to extreme weather events, and rising temperatures and sea levels. These risks are driven by global environmental dynamics and intensified by Malaysia’s rapid economic trajectory, increasing energy needs, growing consumption, and continued fossil fuel dependence.

oc.parentName: Governance, Participation, Rights and Social Cohesion
oc.name: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
oc.description: This outcome focuses on strengthening governance systems and institutional capacities in line with the international human rights standards and normative frameworks. It reflects the Government’s overarching emphasis, as articulated in the Thirteenth Plan, on institutional reform as a core pillar of Malaysia’s development pathway and its forthcoming HIC transition. In this context, UN support aims to help Malaysia embed and uphold global standards of peace and security, the rule of law, human rights, transparency and accountability across all levels of governance, including as part of the efforts to ensure the achievement of the SDG targets by 2030.

ou.name: Access to inclusive quality and values-based education is improved for all children and young people.
ou.description: This collaborative output addresses two interrelated challenges: gaps in mainstream education, including concerns about quality of attainment and increasing social polarization, and the difficulties faced by some non-citizen children in accessing schooling. This latter group includes undocumented and stateless children (particularly in Sabah) as well as refugees, where civil society and the UN often play a critical role in service provision. These educational disparities have far-reaching implications, given the central role of human capital development in national economic transformation and the importance of education in the socialization of values and promotion of social cohesion.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
ou.name: The healthcare system is more resilient and better capacitated to deliver universal access to care, promote well-being and healthy ageing, and address population-specific risk factors.
ou.description: This collaborative output supports both the strengthening of national health systems and their ability to deliver equitable, quality care across the life cycle for all communities. UN agencies will align their work with Malaysia’s Health White Paper (2023), focusing on the development of a health system that is adequately financed, equitable and affordable. The UN will contribute to system resilience by supporting infrastructure, service continuity and fiscal strategies that balance public health financing with reduced out of pocket costs. Informed by the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, the UN will also assist in building preparedness capacities for future public health emergencies.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
ou.name: The social protection system is strengthened to provide universal coverage throughout the lifecycle, especially for people in vulnerable situations.
ou.description: Malaysia’s social protection system faces two primary challenges: incomplete lifecycle coverage for the general population and inadequate provision for individuals with heightened or overlapping vulnerabilities, such as men and women with disabilities, children, older persons, and people living in poverty. These gaps reduce the system’s capacity to mitigate risks and shocks, enable equitable access and effectively address fragmentation, thereby weakening human capital, limiting inclusive economic growth, and contributing to intergenerational cycles of disadvantage, with adverse impacts on nutrition, health, and well-being.  Malaysia is well-positioned to embrace a progressive universality model in strengthening its Social Protection Floor (SPF), to ensure that all citizens, particularly the most vulnerable populations, have access to essential benefits that secure their fundamental rights to health, income, and well-being.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
ou.name: Food and nutrition systems meet the needs of all people in Malaysia, address undernutrition and obesity, specifically among women, children, and other vulnerable groups.
ou.description:
Malaysia faces a triple burden of malnutrition challenge with the coexistence of undernutrition and stunting, especially among children, alongside rising rates of obesity and micronutrient deficiency. These trends reflect both structural inequities and changing consumption patterns linked to rapid economic growth and urbanization. The burden is not evenly distributed, with significant disparities across geographic regions and population groups, requiring disaggregated, equity-sensitive approaches. 
In response, the UN will support the development of integrated, sustainable, and locally adapted food and nutrition systems and policies. Interventions will promote access to sufficient, affordable, and nutritious food while addressing behavioural, cultural and socioeconomic determinants of poor diets. The UN will also contribute to strengthening national capacities in food systems governance, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, and multi-sector coordination.

ou.parentName: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
ou.name: The labour market provides demand-driven opportunities, enhances women’s economic participation, enables reskilling and upskilling, and protects rights for all with a focus on caregivers, migrant workers, persons with disabilities, youth, and women.
ou.description:
Recognizing the central role of employment in driving inclusive growth, this output supports efforts to address persistent labour market disparities and barriers to decent work. Particular attention is given to the economic participation of women, whose labour force participation continues to lag significantly behind, as well as to groups which are disadvantaged in the labour market. 
UN programming and advocacy will promote gender-responsive labour policies and workplace rights, while supporting the development of a more inclusive and demand-driven skills economy.  This includes strengthening the TVET architecture, ensuing that it is better aligned with the evolving needs of industry, and closing skills gaps, particularly in digital, green, and new technologies. A core focus will be on enhancing productivity and enabling access to higher-value employment for women and youth. 
To advance broader inclusion and equity, UN interventions will support the creation of enabling work environments for persons with disabilities, as well as address the employment challenges faced by informal sector workers and migrants. In addition, the UN will also address systemic drivers of child labour in specific sectors. Environmental sustainability will be promoted as an integral part of this transition, including efforts to green the workplace and mainstream just transition principles across labour market reforms.

ou.parentName: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
ou.name: Productivity and competitiveness, particularly of MSMEs, are enhanced as Malaysia transitions to a digital and green high-income economy with a fair and transparent business environment which promotes SDG-aligned investments
ou.description:
Malaysia’s productivity growth and competitiveness, especially among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) remain constrained by structural and capacity-related challenges. This output focuses on addressing these constraints through targeted support to enhance enterprise performance, enabling broader economic transformation. Interventions will include improved technology transfer, labour reskilling, and better access to finance and trade opportunities. The explicit linking of productivity and competitiveness gains with greener and more inclusive business models will be a dimension of the UN’s approach. 
The UN will seek to deliver this, by supporting the take-up of ESG practices and investments particularly by MSMEs and securing wider SDG compliance via the realignment of business incentives, in particular in the context of the forthcoming National ESG Strategic Plan, a ten-year plan envisioned to take Malaysian business entities beyond ESG compliance, and drive competitive advantage. In the social and governance spheres, this includes the business and human rights agenda, and in the environmental sphere, improving resource and energy efficiency, and facilitating access to new technologies and markets, such as those related to electric vehicles, renewable energy, and artificial intelligence. 

To enable these shifts, the UN will provide technical support for policy reforms aimed at creating a more supportive operating environment, including appropriate incentive structures to encourage improvements in productivity and competitiveness alongside SDG objectives. This involves supporting and accelerating current government reforms and tackling key bottlenecks, particularly to MSME expansion, notably, access to finance and trade opportunities for all sectors, including agri-commodities. The UN’s work will also include supporting the scaling up of (this is as mentioned in RMK13) MSMEs, particularly to access green financing, foster sustainable business practices and enable their integration into global green supply chains.

ou.parentName: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
ou.name: Infrastructures and investments are more equitable, recognizing the needs of urban and rural areas, and communities at risk of being left behind.
ou.description:
Spatial and group-based inequalities, such as between urban and rural areas, core, and peripheral regions and vis a vis groups at risk of being left behind, remain among Malaysia’s most pressing development challenges. Some 75 per cent of the population live in cities, and there is growing urban sprawl and urban-rural gaps.  These disparities undermine inclusive growth and risk constraining the country’s HIC transition. While Government’s efforts are underway to address these imbalances, a more data-driven, inclusive, and spatially sensitive approach is required to ensure more equitable development outcomes. 
In response, the UN will support efforts to strengthen national and subnational data systems and analytical capacities to better identify and track geographic and demographic disparities.  This evidence base will inform more responsive and inclusive policymaking, particularly in relation to infrastructure development, service provision, and public investment. These efforts are especially pertinent to regional and local planning initiatives, addressing spatial disparities.
Indeed, complementing this, the UN programming will promote and enable greater investments in underserved regions and for vulnerable populations. This includes supporting initiatives to reduce rural-urban divides, address disparities between Malaysia’s core and lagging states, and help enhance infrastructure provision and services to groups at risk of being left behind.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Malaysia adopts just, clean energy, low-carbon, gender-responsive and circular economy solutions, including more effectively managed waste and improved regulation of pollution.
ou.description:
This collaborative output addresses both policy formulation and implementation of Malaysia’s green transition. At the policy level, UN support will focus on enhancing climate mitigation and adaptation strategies through the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) framework and national adaptation planning. Particular attention will be given to addressing plastic pollution, particularly within marine areas, and reversing biodiversity loss in vulnerable localities.  
At the operational level, the UN will provide technical assistance on the roll-out of clean energy, low-carbon and just transition policies, as well as policies related to waste management and pollution control. These will include the adoption of climate-adaptive technologies, application of circular economy models, and improved environmental planning and regulation at subnational levels across all sectors. 
Additionally, industry-level efforts will focus on high-impact sectors, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, and electric mobility, while embedding just transition principles to protect workers and communities affected by the ongoing shifts in energy production and consumption.  The UN will advocate for improved environmental stewardship across enterprises, including MSMEs, by promoting low-carbon practices, ESG-aligned investments, and circular economy solutions.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Institutions are strengthened and local communities, particularly indigenous peoples, are empowered to drive sustainable, gender-responsive and inclusive natural resource and biodiversity management, and nature-based solutions.
ou.description:
This output focuses on enhancing institutional capacity and community empowerment to support effective and equitable environmental stewardship. At the federal level, the UN will provide technical assistance to strengthen leadership, coordination, and policy implementation on urban environmental management. At the subnational level, support will be tailored to specific needs of local governments, including improving spatial planning and delivering tailored local solutions related to waste management, air quality and urban living conditions, including the preservation and provision of green spaces.
UN programming will contribute to systems strengthening and building the capacities of institutions to decarbonize, restore and protect eco-systems, and promote disaster resilience through risk-assessment and risk-proofing of infrastructure and investments. This will include strengthening of climate data for evidence-informed decision-making and environmental governance. Special emphasis will be on building the capacity of local governments to manage municipal, chemical and biomedical waste, improve the urban environment and living conditions, and integrate pollution-related risks into local public health frameworks. 
The UN will also work with the Government to leverage global and regional climate and biodiversity knowledge through inter-governmental exchange and South-South cooperation. Cross-border environmental challenges such as haze pollution, waste trafficking, and marine pollution caused by disposal of plastic debris in the ocean will be also addressed in partnerships with national and regional stakeholders.
Finally, UN agencies will seek to protect the rights of the resource-dependent communities, including indigenous peoples and local communities, promoting equitable and sustainable access to natural resources, ensuring adherence to Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) standards. The UN will also explore and leverage the potential of traditional knowledge systems to deliver better environmental and resource management at the local level.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Resilience of communities, women and children, and other groups most vulnerable to environmental hazards, shocks, and disasters, is strengthened by enhancing adaptive capacities and meaningful participation in decision-making and solutions.
ou.description:
At both the strategic and operational levels, the UN will support policy and programming measures that promote greater resilience to environmental and climate-related shocks to all communities. This will include enabling policy development at the federal and state levels to advance climate-adaptive investments, strengthened climate-resilient social services and to facilitate and incentivize the building of resilience within society more broadly. UN interventions will include assisting with the adoption of new techniques within government (risk-assessment/risk proofing) and applying fiscal and regulatory instruments to manage and mitigate environmental risks. The UN will seek to enable effective coordination across levels of government and across localities, recognizing the variability of threats and vulnerabilities. 
Through partnerships with civil society, the UN will reach out to local communities to engage them in greening workplace and household practices and promoting locally tailored measures to mitigate shocks and enhance self-adaptation. Special attention will be given to the differentiated vulnerabilities of the groups most at risk, especially women, low-income households, and those facing multiple forms of exclusion. Targeted support will also focus on communities in vulnerable and geographically remote areas, including indigenous peoples and those which are resource-dependent (e.g., fishing communities).

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: People, especially women and children, benefit from justice and human rights protections as institutions and legal frameworks are aligned with international normative standards and function effectively.
ou.description:
The UN will leverage its normative mandate to advocate for the realization of human rights for all, with a focus on vulnerable groups . Efforts will include advocacy for Malaysia’s accession to the six-core international human rights treaties not yet ratified, and for the reduction of reservations on the three ratified treaties (CEDAW, CRC and CRPD). UNCT will promote women’s participation in social, economic, and political life, advocate against practices that harm women and girls, and support mainstreaming of gender equality and women’s empowerment in development plans and M&E frameworks. The UN will also support the implementation of existing international commitments and obligations on women, peace and security.
Through partnerships with the private sector, the UN will promote human rights in the workplace and in the provision of goods and services, building on the work already underway during the previous CF cycle.  Complementary efforts will support the endorsement and implementation of ILO labour conventions, ensuring alignment with international labour standards.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: Institutions and participatory mechanisms are strengthened to effectively promote inclusion and social cohesion and respond to all forms of violence (including gender-based violence), crime, exploitation, stigmatization, discrimination, and harmful practices.
ou.description:
Recognizing the Government’s strong commitment to social harmony and national unity, the UN will contribute to the implementation of the National Unity Policy and Blueprint 2021-2030 to strengthen inter-ethnic relations, social cohesion, and trust by engaging with diverse communities and promoting interactions and exchange. Programming will support dialogue and promote innovative channels for direct engagement, with particular emphasis on women, youth, and persons with disabilities, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation at all levels of decision-making and governance. 
The UN will also partner with media and civil society stakeholders to promote digital citizenship and media literacy, to counter divisive narratives, xenophobia, hate speech and misogyny and to combat discrimination and stigma.  Interventions will also seek to strengthen multisectoral responses to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, children, and persons with disabilities.
UN agencies will continue to advocate for the rights and protection of refugees, stateless people, and undocumented populations, including tailored support to mitigate stigma and exclusion. Specific attention will be given to migrant workers, including advocacy on rights, welfare, and access to services and remedies. Given the scale of the challenge, particular focus will be placed on Sabah, where a significant share of the stateless and undocumented population resides, to support durable policy responses.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: Institutions are more accountable, transparent and gender-responsive, implement innovative evidence-based policies and laws at national and subnational levels, and prevent and combat corruption and transnational crime.
ou.description:
The UN will support efforts to enhance institutional accountability, transparency, and responsiveness at all levels of government. This will include promoting international benchmarking, peer learning, and the adaptation of innovative governance approaches. The UN will advocate for strengthening of state and local government capacities to enhance service delivery and local development. This will be complemented by in-situ programming, particularly in urban areas, and SDG-based local planning, budgeting, and implementation monitoring. This will be enhanced by UN support to national authorities, including the Department of Statistics of Malaysia (DOSM), in generating, accessing, and utilizing SDG-related and other data, disaggregated by group characteristics (specifically including gender) and locality, to strengthen evidenced-based policymaking. National evaluation capacities will also be strengthened.
Support to anti-corruption efforts will include both prevention and effective enforcement of laws. The UN will promote innovative approaches harnessing digitalization and new technologies, open budgeting initiatives, while also advancing traditional accountability mechanisms such as the right to information, public reporting of corruption, and whistle-blower protections.

UN agencies will support law enforcement, including enhancing cross-border cooperation on cybercrime investigation and intelligence sharing among law enforcement agencies, as well as provide recommendations for policy development, to prevent, and counter organized and transnational crime, including trafficking in persons, smuggling of drugs, cybercrime, scamming operations and illicit financial flows.

oc.parentName: Economic Transformation for Inclusive and Sustainable Prosperity
oc.name: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
oc.description: The outcome statement for SPA 2 focuses on inclusive and sustainable economic transformation. oc.parentName: Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
