oc.parentName: Governance, Participation, Rights and Social Cohesion
oc.name: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
oc.description: This outcome focuses on strengthening governance systems and institutional capacities in line with the international human rights standards and normative frameworks. ou.name: Access to inclusive quality and values-based education is improved for all children and young people.
ou.description: This collaborative output addresses two interrelated challenges: gaps in mainstream education, including concerns about quality of attainment and increasing social polarization, and the difficulties faced by some non-citizen children in accessing schooling. ou.parentName: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
ou.name: The healthcare system is more resilient and better capacitated to deliver universal access to care, promote well-being and healthy ageing, and address population-specific risk factors.
ou.description: This collaborative output supports both the strengthening of national health systems and their ability to deliver equitable, quality care across the life cycle for all communities. UN agencies will align their work with Malaysia’s Health White Paper (2023), focusing on the development of a health system that is adequately financed, equitable and affordable. The UN will contribute to system resilience by supporting infrastructure, service continuity and fiscal strategies that balance public health financing with reduced out of pocket costs. Informed by the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, the UN will also assist in building preparedness capacities for future public health emergencies.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
ou.name: The social protection system is strengthened to provide universal coverage throughout the lifecycle, especially for people in vulnerable situations.
ou.description: Malaysia’s social protection system faces two primary challenges: incomplete lifecycle coverage for the general population and inadequate provision for individuals with heightened or overlapping vulnerabilities, such as men and women with disabilities, children, older persons, and people living in poverty. These gaps reduce the system’s capacity to mitigate risks and shocks, enable equitable access and effectively address fragmentation, thereby weakening human capital, limiting inclusive economic growth, and contributing to intergenerational cycles of disadvantage, with adverse impacts on nutrition, health, and well-being.  Malaysia is well-positioned to embrace a progressive universality model in strengthening its Social Protection Floor (SPF), to ensure that all citizens, particularly the most vulnerable populations, have access to essential benefits that secure their fundamental rights to health, income, and well-being.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people living in Malaysia, particularly those in vulnerable situations, have access to high-quality, rights-based, gender-responsive, and disability-inclusive social services.
ou.name: Food and nutrition systems meet the needs of all people in Malaysia, address undernutrition and obesity, specifically among women, children, and other vulnerable groups.
ou.description:
Malaysia faces a triple burden of malnutrition challenge with the coexistence of undernutrition and stunting, especially among children, alongside rising rates of obesity and micronutrient deficiency. These trends reflect both structural inequities and changing consumption patterns linked to rapid economic growth and urbanization. The burden is not evenly distributed, with significant disparities across geographic regions and population groups, requiring disaggregated, equity-sensitive approaches. 
In response, the UN will support the development of integrated, sustainable, and locally adapted food and nutrition systems and policies. Interventions will promote access to sufficient, affordable, and nutritious food while addressing behavioural, cultural and socioeconomic determinants of poor diets. The UN will also contribute to strengthening national capacities in food systems governance, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, and multi-sector coordination.

ou.parentName: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
ou.name: The labour market provides demand-driven opportunities, enhances women’s economic participation, enables reskilling and upskilling, and protects rights for all with a focus on caregivers, migrant workers, persons with disabilities, youth, and women.
ou.description:
Recognizing the central role of employment in driving inclusive growth, this output supports efforts to address persistent labour market disparities and barriers to decent work. Particular attention is given to the economic participation of women, whose labour force participation continues to lag significantly behind, as well as to groups which are disadvantaged in the labour market. 
UN programming and advocacy will promote gender-responsive labour policies and workplace rights, while supporting the development of a more inclusive and demand-driven skills economy.  This includes strengthening the TVET architecture, ensuing that it is better aligned with the evolving needs of industry, and closing skills gaps, particularly in digital, green, and new technologies. A core focus will be on enhancing productivity and enabling access to higher-value employment for women and youth. 
To advance broader inclusion and equity, UN interventions will support the creation of enabling work environments for persons with disabilities, as well as address the employment challenges faced by informal sector workers and migrants. In addition, the UN will also address systemic drivers of child labour in specific sectors. Environmental sustainability will be promoted as an integral part of this transition, including efforts to green the workplace and mainstream just transition principles across labour market reforms.

ou.parentName: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
ou.name: Productivity and competitiveness, particularly of MSMEs, are enhanced as Malaysia transitions to a digital and green high-income economy with a fair and transparent business environment which promotes SDG-aligned investments
ou.description:
Malaysia’s productivity growth and competitiveness, especially among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) remain constrained by structural and capacity-related challenges. This output focuses on addressing these constraints through targeted support to enhance enterprise performance, enabling broader economic transformation. Interventions will include improved technology transfer, labour reskilling, and better access to finance and trade opportunities. The explicit linking of productivity and competitiveness gains with greener and more inclusive business models will be a dimension of the UN’s approach. 
The UN will seek to deliver this, by supporting the take-up of ESG practices and investments particularly by MSMEs and securing wider SDG compliance via the realignment of business incentives, in particular in the context of the forthcoming National ESG Strategic Plan, a ten-year plan envisioned to take Malaysian business entities beyond ESG compliance, and drive competitive advantage. In the social and governance spheres, this includes the business and human rights agenda, and in the environmental sphere, improving resource and energy efficiency, and facilitating access to new technologies and markets, such as those related to electric vehicles, renewable energy, and artificial intelligence. 

To enable these shifts, the UN will provide technical support for policy reforms aimed at creating a more supportive operating environment, including appropriate incentive structures to encourage improvements in productivity and competitiveness alongside SDG objectives. This involves supporting and accelerating current government reforms and tackling key bottlenecks, particularly to MSME expansion, notably, access to finance and trade opportunities for all sectors, including agri-commodities. The UN’s work will also include supporting the scaling up of (this is as mentioned in RMK13) MSMEs, particularly to access green financing, foster sustainable business practices and enable their integration into global green supply chains.

ou.parentName: By 2030, Malaysia’s economy is resilient, environmentally sustainable, and delivers growth and opportunities for all, leveraging the contributions of women, youth, and people in lagging regions.
ou.name: Infrastructures and investments are more equitable, recognizing the needs of urban and rural areas, and communities at risk of being left behind.
ou.description:
Spatial and group-based inequalities, such as between urban and rural areas, core, and peripheral regions and vis a vis groups at risk of being left behind, remain among Malaysia’s most pressing development challenges. Some 75 per cent of the population live in cities, and there is growing urban sprawl and urban-rural gaps.  These disparities undermine inclusive growth and risk constraining the country’s HIC transition. While Government’s efforts are underway to address these imbalances, a more data-driven, inclusive, and spatially sensitive approach is required to ensure more equitable development outcomes. 
In response, the UN will support efforts to strengthen national and subnational data systems and analytical capacities to better identify and track geographic and demographic disparities.  This evidence base will inform more responsive and inclusive policymaking, particularly in relation to infrastructure development, service provision, and public investment. These efforts are especially pertinent to regional and local planning initiatives, addressing spatial disparities.
Indeed, complementing this, the UN programming will promote and enable greater investments in underserved regions and for vulnerable populations. This includes supporting initiatives to reduce rural-urban divides, address disparities between Malaysia’s core and lagging states, and help enhance infrastructure provision and services to groups at risk of being left behind.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Malaysia adopts just, clean energy, low-carbon, gender-responsive and circular economy solutions, including more effectively managed waste and improved regulation of pollution.
ou.description:
This collaborative output addresses both policy formulation and implementation of Malaysia’s green transition. At the policy level, UN support will focus on enhancing climate mitigation and adaptation strategies through the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) framework and national adaptation planning. Particular attention will be given to addressing plastic pollution, particularly within marine areas, and reversing biodiversity loss in vulnerable localities.  
At the operational level, the UN will provide technical assistance on the roll-out of clean energy, low-carbon and just transition policies, as well as policies related to waste management and pollution control. These will include the adoption of climate-adaptive technologies, application of circular economy models, and improved environmental planning and regulation at subnational levels across all sectors. 
Additionally, industry-level efforts will focus on high-impact sectors, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, and electric mobility, while embedding just transition principles to protect workers and communities affected by the ongoing shifts in energy production and consumption.  The UN will advocate for improved environmental stewardship across enterprises, including MSMEs, by promoting low-carbon practices, ESG-aligned investments, and circular economy solutions.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Institutions are strengthened and local communities, particularly indigenous peoples, are empowered to drive sustainable, gender-responsive and inclusive natural resource and biodiversity management, and nature-based solutions.
ou.description:
This output focuses on enhancing institutional capacity and community empowerment to support effective and equitable environmental stewardship. At the federal level, the UN will provide technical assistance to strengthen leadership, coordination, and policy implementation on urban environmental management. At the subnational level, support will be tailored to specific needs of local governments, including improving spatial planning and delivering tailored local solutions related to waste management, air quality and urban living conditions, including the preservation and provision of green spaces.
UN programming will contribute to systems strengthening and building the capacities of institutions to decarbonize, restore and protect eco-systems, and promote disaster resilience through risk-assessment and risk-proofing of infrastructure and investments. This will include strengthening of climate data for evidence-informed decision-making and environmental governance. Special emphasis will be on building the capacity of local governments to manage municipal, chemical and biomedical waste, improve the urban environment and living conditions, and integrate pollution-related risks into local public health frameworks. 
The UN will also work with the Government to leverage global and regional climate and biodiversity knowledge through inter-governmental exchange and South-South cooperation. Cross-border environmental challenges such as haze pollution, waste trafficking, and marine pollution caused by disposal of plastic debris in the ocean will be also addressed in partnerships with national and regional stakeholders.
Finally, UN agencies will seek to protect the rights of the resource-dependent communities, including indigenous peoples and local communities, promoting equitable and sustainable access to natural resources, ensuring adherence to Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) standards. The UN will also explore and leverage the potential of traditional knowledge systems to deliver better environmental and resource management at the local level.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Resilience of communities, women and children, and other groups most vulnerable to environmental hazards, shocks, and disasters, is strengthened by enhancing adaptive capacities and meaningful participation in decision-making and solutions.
ou.description:
At both the strategic and operational levels, the UN will support policy and programming measures that promote greater resilience to environmental and climate-related shocks to all communities. This will include enabling policy development at the federal and state levels to advance climate-adaptive investments, strengthened climate-resilient social services and to facilitate and incentivize the building of resilience within society more broadly. UN interventions will include assisting with the adoption of new techniques within government (risk-assessment/risk proofing) and applying fiscal and regulatory instruments to manage and mitigate environmental risks. The UN will seek to enable effective coordination across levels of government and across localities, recognizing the variability of threats and vulnerabilities. 
Through partnerships with civil society, the UN will reach out to local communities to engage them in greening workplace and household practices and promoting locally tailored measures to mitigate shocks and enhance self-adaptation. Special attention will be given to the differentiated vulnerabilities of the groups most at risk, especially women, low-income households, and those facing multiple forms of exclusion. Targeted support will also focus on communities in vulnerable and geographically remote areas, including indigenous peoples and those which are resource-dependent (e.g., fishing communities).

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: People, especially women and children, benefit from justice and human rights protections as institutions and legal frameworks are aligned with international normative standards and function effectively.
ou.description:
The UN will leverage its normative mandate to advocate for the realization of human rights for all, with a focus on vulnerable groups . Efforts will include advocacy for Malaysia’s accession to the six-core international human rights treaties not yet ratified, and for the reduction of reservations on the three ratified treaties (CEDAW, CRC and CRPD). UNCT will promote women’s participation in social, economic, and political life, advocate against practices that harm women and girls, and support mainstreaming of gender equality and women’s empowerment in development plans and M&E frameworks. The UN will also support the implementation of existing international commitments and obligations on women, peace and security.
Through partnerships with the private sector, the UN will promote human rights in the workplace and in the provision of goods and services, building on the work already underway during the previous CF cycle.  Complementary efforts will support the endorsement and implementation of ILO labour conventions, ensuring alignment with international labour standards.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: Institutions and participatory mechanisms are strengthened to effectively promote inclusion and social cohesion and respond to all forms of violence (including gender-based violence), crime, exploitation, stigmatization, discrimination, and harmful practices.
ou.description:
Recognizing the Government’s strong commitment to social harmony and national unity, the UN will contribute to the implementation of the National Unity Policy and Blueprint 2021-2030 to strengthen inter-ethnic relations, social cohesion, and trust by engaging with diverse communities and promoting interactions and exchange. Programming will support dialogue and promote innovative channels for direct engagement, with particular emphasis on women, youth, and persons with disabilities, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation at all levels of decision-making and governance. 
The UN will also partner with media and civil society stakeholders to promote digital citizenship and media literacy, to counter divisive narratives, xenophobia, hate speech and misogyny and to combat discrimination and stigma.  Interventions will also seek to strengthen multisectoral responses to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, children, and persons with disabilities.
UN agencies will continue to advocate for the rights and protection of refugees, stateless people, and undocumented populations, including tailored support to mitigate stigma and exclusion. Specific attention will be given to migrant workers, including advocacy on rights, welfare, and access to services and remedies. Given the scale of the challenge, particular focus will be placed on Sabah, where a significant share of the stateless and undocumented population resides, to support durable policy responses.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: Institutions are more accountable, transparent and gender-responsive, implement innovative evidence-based policies and laws at national and subnational levels, and prevent and combat corruption and transnational crime.
ou.description:
The UN will support efforts to enhance institutional accountability, transparency, and responsiveness at all levels of government. This will include promoting international benchmarking, peer learning, and the adaptation of innovative governance approaches. The UN will advocate for strengthening of state and local government capacities to enhance service delivery and local development. This will be complemented by in-situ programming, particularly in urban areas, and SDG-based local planning, budgeting, and implementation monitoring. This will be enhanced by UN support to national authorities, including the Department of Statistics of Malaysia (DOSM), in generating, accessing, and utilizing SDG-related and other data, disaggregated by group characteristics (specifically including gender) and locality, to strengthen evidenced-based policymaking. National evaluation capacities will also be strengthened.
Support to anti-corruption efforts will include both prevention and effective enforcement of laws. The UN will promote innovative approaches harnessing digitalization and new technologies, open budgeting initiatives, while also advancing traditional accountability mechanisms such as the right to information, public reporting of corruption, and whistle-blower protections.
The UN system will also contribute to efficient, resilient, and inclusive delivery of public services by enabling digital governance through capacity building, and the transfer of technology and know- how. UN agencies will support law enforcement, including enhancing cross-border cooperation on cybercrime investigation and intelligence sharing among law enforcement agencies, as well as provide recommendations for policy development, to prevent, and counter organized and transnational crime, including trafficking in persons, smuggling of drugs, cybercrime, scamming operations and illicit financial flows.

ou.name: Malaysia adopts just, clean energy, low-carbon, gender-responsive and circular economy solutions, including more effectively managed waste and improved regulation of pollution.
ou.description:
This collaborative output addresses both policy formulation and implementation of Malaysia’s green transition. At the policy level, UN support will focus on enhancing climate mitigation and adaptation strategies through the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) framework and national adaptation planning. Particular attention will be given to addressing plastic pollution, particularly within marine areas, and reversing biodiversity loss in vulnerable localities.  
At the operational level, the UN will provide technical assistance on the roll-out of clean energy, low-carbon and just transition policies, as well as policies related to waste management and pollution control. These will include the adoption of climate-adaptive technologies, application of circular economy models, and improved environmental planning and regulation at subnational levels across all sectors. 
Additionally, industry-level efforts will focus on high-impact sectors, such as renewable energy, energy efficiency, and electric mobility, while embedding just transition principles to protect workers and communities affected by the ongoing shifts in energy production and consumption.  The UN will advocate for improved environmental stewardship across enterprises, including MSMEs, by promoting low-carbon practices, ESG-aligned investments, and circular economy solutions.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Institutions are strengthened and local communities, particularly indigenous peoples, are empowered to drive sustainable, gender-responsive and inclusive natural resource and biodiversity management, and nature-based solutions.
ou.description:
This output focuses on enhancing institutional capacity and community empowerment to support effective and equitable environmental stewardship. At the federal level, the UN will provide technical assistance to strengthen leadership, coordination, and policy implementation on urban environmental management. At the subnational level, support will be tailored to specific needs of local governments, including improving spatial planning and delivering tailored local solutions related to waste management, air quality and urban living conditions, including the preservation and provision of green spaces.
UN programming will contribute to systems strengthening and building the capacities of institutions to decarbonize, restore and protect eco-systems, and promote disaster resilience through risk-assessment and risk-proofing of infrastructure and investments. This will include strengthening of climate data for evidence-informed decision-making and environmental governance. Special emphasis will be on building the capacity of local governments to manage municipal, chemical and biomedical waste, improve the urban environment and living conditions, and integrate pollution-related risks into local public health frameworks. 
The UN will also work with the Government to leverage global and regional climate and biodiversity knowledge through inter-governmental exchange and South-South cooperation. Cross-border environmental challenges such as haze pollution, waste trafficking, and marine pollution caused by disposal of plastic debris in the ocean will be also addressed in partnerships with national and regional stakeholders.
Finally, UN agencies will seek to protect the rights of the resource-dependent communities, including indigenous peoples and local communities, promoting equitable and sustainable access to natural resources, ensuring adherence to Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) standards. The UN will also explore and leverage the potential of traditional knowledge systems to deliver better environmental and resource management at the local level.

ou.parentName: By 2030, natural resources are managed sustainably, biodiversity is preserved, pollution is reduced, and climate action is enhanced towards delivering greater resilience and national climate change commitments
ou.name: Resilience of communities, women and children, and other groups most vulnerable to environmental hazards, shocks, and disasters, is strengthened by enhancing adaptive capacities and meaningful participation in decision-making and solutions.
ou.description:
At both the strategic and operational levels, the UN will support policy and programming measures that promote greater resilience to environmental and climate-related shocks to all communities. This will include enabling policy development at the federal and state levels to advance climate-adaptive investments, strengthened climate-resilient social services and to facilitate and incentivize the building of resilience within society more broadly. UN interventions will include assisting with the adoption of new techniques within government (risk-assessment/risk proofing) and applying fiscal and regulatory instruments to manage and mitigate environmental risks. The UN will seek to enable effective coordination across levels of government and across localities, recognizing the variability of threats and vulnerabilities. 
Through partnerships with civil society, the UN will reach out to local communities to engage them in greening workplace and household practices and promoting locally tailored measures to mitigate shocks and enhance self-adaptation. Special attention will be given to the differentiated vulnerabilities of the groups most at risk, especially women, low-income households, and those facing multiple forms of exclusion. Targeted support will also focus on communities in vulnerable and geographically remote areas, including indigenous peoples and those which are resource-dependent (e.g., fishing communities).

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: People, especially women and children, benefit from justice and human rights protections as institutions and legal frameworks are aligned with international normative standards and function effectively.
ou.description:
The UN will leverage its normative mandate to advocate for the realization of human rights for all, with a focus on vulnerable groups . Efforts will include advocacy for Malaysia’s accession to the six-core international human rights treaties not yet ratified, and for the reduction of reservations on the three ratified treaties (CEDAW, CRC and CRPD). UNCT will promote women’s participation in social, economic, and political life, advocate against practices that harm women and girls, and support mainstreaming of gender equality and women’s empowerment in development plans and M&E frameworks. The UN will also support the implementation of existing international commitments and obligations on women, peace and security.
Through partnerships with the private sector, the UN will promote human rights in the workplace and in the provision of goods and services, building on the work already underway during the previous CF cycle.  Complementary efforts will support the endorsement and implementation of ILO labour conventions, ensuring alignment with international labour standards.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: Institutions and participatory mechanisms are strengthened to effectively promote inclusion and social cohesion and respond to all forms of violence (including gender-based violence), crime, exploitation, stigmatization, discrimination, and harmful practices.
ou.description:
Recognizing the Government’s strong commitment to social harmony and national unity, the UN will contribute to the implementation of the National Unity Policy and Blueprint 2021-2030 to strengthen inter-ethnic relations, social cohesion, and trust by engaging with diverse communities and promoting interactions and exchange. Programming will support dialogue and promote innovative channels for direct engagement, with particular emphasis on women, youth, and persons with disabilities, ensuring their meaningful participation and representation at all levels of decision-making and governance. 
The UN will also partner with media and civil society stakeholders to promote digital citizenship and media literacy, to counter divisive narratives, xenophobia, hate speech and misogyny and to combat discrimination and stigma.  Interventions will also seek to strengthen multisectoral responses to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, children, and persons with disabilities.
UN agencies will continue to advocate for the rights and protection of refugees, stateless people, and undocumented populations, including tailored support to mitigate stigma and exclusion. Specific attention will be given to migrant workers, including advocacy on rights, welfare, and access to services and remedies. Given the scale of the challenge, particular focus will be placed on Sabah, where a significant share of the stateless and undocumented population resides, to support durable policy responses.

ou.parentName: By 2030, all people in Malaysia enjoy human rights and live in a safe, inclusive, and cohesive society, supported by accountable and transparent public institutions which ensure coordinated, evidence-based and participatory policymaking.
ou.name: Institutions are more accountable, transparent and gender-responsive, implement innovative evidence-based policies and laws at national and subnational levels, and prevent and combat corruption and transnational crime.
ou.description:
The UN will support efforts to enhance institutional accountability, transparency, and responsiveness at all levels of government. This will include promoting international benchmarking, peer learning, and the adaptation of innovative governance approaches. The UN will advocate for strengthening of state and local government capacities to enhance service delivery and local development. This will be complemented by in-situ programming, particularly in urban areas, and SDG-based local planning, budgeting, and implementation monitoring. This will be enhanced by UN support to national authorities, including the Department of Statistics of Malaysia (DOSM), in generating, accessing, and utilizing SDG-related and other data, disaggregated by group characteristics (specifically including gender) and locality, to strengthen evidenced-based policymaking. National evaluation capacities will also be strengthened.
Support to anti-corruption efforts will include both prevention and effective enforcement of laws. The UN will promote innovative approaches harnessing digitalization and new technologies, open budgeting initiatives, while also advancing traditional accountability mechanisms such as the right to information, public reporting of corruption, and whistle-blower protections.
The UN system will also contribute to efficient, resilient, and inclusive delivery of public services by enabling digital governance through capacity building, and the transfer of technology and know- how. UN agencies will support law enforcement, including enhancing cross-border cooperation on cybercrime investigation and intelligence sharing among law enforcement agencies, as well as provide recommendations for policy development, to prevent, and counter organized and transnational crime, including trafficking in persons, smuggling of drugs, cybercrime, scamming operations and illicit financial flows.

sp.name: Strategic Priority 1: Sustained & Inclusive Economic Growth & Development
sp.description:
Prosperity Pillar: Sustained & Inclusive Economic Growth & Development
People  living in Nigeria have sustained inclusive economic growth and development that provides equitable opportunities for decent employment and livelihoods 

The aim is to improve the underlying drivers of sustained and inclusive economic growth. The areas of focus include:
1)  improving productivity and competitiveness across various sectors especially relating to helping Nigeria diversify its exports
2) creating decent job opportunities and employments for all.  This is to cover but not limited to digitization and digital transformation, skills development  and entrepreneurship
3) Improving social protection that is gender-responsive, age-friendly and shock responsive
4) supporting a policy data driven environment for improved and sustainable growth

sp.name: Strategic Priority 2: Clean Energy, Food Systems, Environmental Protection & Climate Change Resilience
sp.description:
Planet Pillar: Environmental Protection & Climate Change Resilience
People living in Nigeria particularly the most vulnerable have equitable access to affordable clean energy, enjoy sustainable food systems, healthy and clean environmental conditions and increased resilience to climate change and disasters.

The priority area highlights three key outcomes which are:
1) Improved food security and nutrition, environmental sustainability, and sustainable natural resources management.
2) Improved management of climate change risks and building resilience to climate induced shocks
 3) Inclusive policies and practices for resilience and disaster risk management (DRM)

sp.name: Strategic Priority 3: Inclusive & Equitable Human Capital Development & Wellbeing
sp.description:
People Pillar:  Inclusive & Equitable Human Capital Development & Well-being
People living in Nigeria have inclusive and equitable human development and well-being

The strategic pillar focuses on ensuring that people living in Nigeria have inclusive and equitable human development and well-being with a focus on the health and education of people in Nigeria and the access to quality basic services.

The priority area highlights three key outcomes which ensure that people living in Nigeria have:
1) Equitable access to, and use integrated, comprehensive, high-quality, people centered health services towards attaining Universal Health coverage
2) Equitable access and use of quality education system that delivers an inclusive education for learning and transferable skills
3) Equitable and affordable access to safely managed water and sanitation facilities, and practice safe hygiene and behaviors

sp.name: Strategic Priority 4: Governance, Peace, Security, Access to Justice & Rule of Law
sp.description:
Peace Pillar:  Governance, Peace, Security, Access to Justice & Rule of Law
People living in Nigeria have more inclusive, participatory, transparent and gender equitable governance, gender responsive justice and human rights systems at all levels that promote peaceful, inclusive and a cohesive society.

The priority area highlights three key outcomes which ensure that:
1) people living in Nigeria especially the most vulnerable, benefit from peace and security, and protection from conflict violence, and crime through strengthen capacity and infrastructures
2) people living in Nigeria have access to a more accountable, transparent, and gender responsive, and inclusive governance and justice system for the realization of human rights 
3) gender equality and human rights of women, youth, older persons and other marginalized groups including persons with disabilities in Nigeria are enhanced.

sp.name: Sustained Essential Services
sp.description:
Sustaining and improving equitable and inclusive access to essential, people-centred social services is crucial for people in Afghanistan — particularly the most vulnerable and marginalized — to improve their well-being, break the pattern of intergenerational poverty, support gender equity and equality, strengthen resilience to life-cycle risks, reduce vulnerability to shocks, and contribute to the country’s recovery. Progress towards this outcome will depend on the extent to which essential health, nutrition, education, employment, water, sanitation, hygiene, social protection, and protection services are accessible to all, affordable, and can be delivered free from all forms of discrimination.

Essential service providers, including women, will require the operational access, knowledge, and skills so that service delivery meets minimum quality standards. Essential infrastructure and facilities should be improved and accessible to all — including persons with disabilities, gender-responsive, adequate, safe, and culturally and age-appropriate and have the requisite infrastructure and supplies at the point of delivery. The critical foundations, capacities, and systems built over the past two decades will also need to be sustained and strengthened. As such, the UN, in coordination with its partners, will focus their collective support towards the following areas.

sp.name: Economic Opportunities and Resilient Livelihoods
sp.description:
Addressing Afghanistan’s chronic economic challenges will require community-level resilience strengthening towards shocks and stressors — including natural hazards and economic shocks — and bottom-up and inclusive economic recovery that creates decent jobs, raises incomes, and increases agricultural and industrial production. This will require greater macroeconomic and fiscal stability and an enabling environment that facilitates economic growth and creates more decent work opportunities, especially for excluded groups such as women. Private sector-led economic development will depend on a more favourable policy and regulatory environment, as well as the availability of the requisite business development services, access to finance, and infrastructure that stimulates investment and growth. Functional tripartite forums with the engagement of trade unions and employers’ associations will be required to ensure decent work and compliance of working conditions with labour standards. Strengthening a labour force that meets labour market needs will require investments in skilled personnel to deliver necessary market-relevant knowledge and skills.

More efficient, sustainable, and resilient agribusiness, handcraft, and garment value chains underpinned by sustainable natural resource management will support economic opportunities for rural livelihoods and contribute towards improved food security. Employment-intensive and climate-resilient approaches to the rehabilitation and construction of community assets will create jobs and build resilience. Additionally, the capacities of communities, ecosystems, food systems, and institutions across the country will also need to be strengthened to anticipate, absorb, manage, and adapt to natural shocks, including climate-related shocks and stressors, especially floods and droughts.

However, the country’s potential can only be realized if restrictions on women’s rights related to mobility, full participation in the economy, and education are removed and their participation is promoted and sustained. The UN, with its partners, will work in the following areas towards achievement of these goals.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, particularly the most marginalized, can equitably access essential services that meet minimum quality standards.
ou.name: Output 1.1: Health and nutrition systems have improved and resilient capacities and resources to deliver accessible, affordable, gender- and age-responsive, shock responsive, and culturally acceptable essential healthcare and nutrition services that prioritize the most vulnerable.
ou.description:
UN health and nutrition partners will strengthen collaboration and strategic partnership, including proactive information sharing, joint planning, and programming, to minimize preventable morbidities, mortality, and improve well-being, especially among women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable population groups.

Delivery of essential healthcare and nutrition services will be strengthened and expanded in underserved areas to reach vulnerable people at each stage of the life cycle, with emphasis on improved access, quality, and patient safety, especially for women and girls. Investments will prioritize evidence-based, effective maternal, child, and adolescent health and nutrition treatment, prevention, and promotion interventions.

Essential foundations of the public health systems will be sustained and strengthened, including progressive transitional strategies and guidelines, trained human resources (with a focus on sustaining and increasing female staff), small-scale critical infrastructure (such as solarization and water, sanitation, and hygiene), models of care (including area-based referral pathways), medical commodities, medicines and vaccines, a functional health information system, monitoring and surveillance, and more effective sub-national coordination. Capacities will be reinforced to prevent, detect, and respond to disease outbreaks and other health and nutrition shocks. The UN will advocate for harmonization and alignment of financial resources toward national health and nutrition priorities and increase transparency, accountability, predictability, adaptability, and efficiency of funding.

Development of policies, strategies, and guidelines in accordance with international standards and best practices may be supported while mechanisms for surveillance, monitoring, and periodic surveys will be enhanced.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, particularly the most marginalized, can equitably access essential services that meet minimum quality standards.
ou.name: Output 1.2: Formal and non-formal public, private, and community-based education systems are better able to sustain and increase access to inclusive, safe, and quality education opportunities for girls, boys, youth, and adults — especially girls and young women — across all levels of education.
ou.description:
UN partners will prioritize interventions at basic education (primary and secondary), technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and higher education levels through support to coordinated education initiatives. These initiatives will form a bridge from humanitarian response to longer-term, inclusive development to ensure continuity of learning while exploring alternative education modalities for those not reached by these initiatives. Targeted support will be provided to the formal and non-formal private and public education system with a focus on quality, monitoring, evidence generation, and planning. Advocacy at all levels for the right to education, especially for girls and women, will be prioritized.

To enable sustainable pathways, the UN will facilitate interventions that include, but not be limited to, in-service teacher/lecturer training and professional development (including for women), integrated school rehabilitation, provision of literacy, school feeding programmes, numeracy and skills development opportunities, alternative education modalities for out-of-school children and youth, particularly girls, strengthening of school management Shuras — including the participation of women in these mechanisms — direct targeted support to basic and tertiary education students, improvement of learning assessments, and stakeholder capacity building on key sectoral functions, including evidence-based planning and monitoring. If education delivery by and for women and girls can be ensured, greater support to school-level management and oversight by sub-national education administrators may be possible, along with larger infrastructure work.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, particularly the most marginalized, can equitably access essential services that meet minimum quality standards.
ou.name: Output 1.3: Stakeholders at national and subnational level are better able to manage and provide access to equitable, gender responsive, sustainable, climate resilient, and safe drinking water, improved sanitation, and positive hygiene practices in rural and poor urban communities.
ou.description:
In collaboration with humanitarian partners, the UN will adopt a two-pronged approach that delivers emergency water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) support while simultaneously implementing longer-term, sustainable solutions that tackle the drivers of WASH-related humanitarian needs.

In coordination with water management and infrastructure-related activities under Strategic Priority 2, the UN will prioritize the expansion of access to safe drinking water through the rehabilitation, continuous operation, maintenance, and expansion of water infrastructure in rural and urban locations (enabling through the provision of energy access/services). The UN will also support the implementation of integrated water resources management solutions at all levels to substantially increase water-use efficiency and ensure sustainable withdrawals and supply of freshwater to address water scarcity.

Efforts will also be expanded in tackling the poor availability of sanitation — one of the main causes of disease outbreaks in Afghanistan — through the provision of improved gender-responsive sanitation services and facilities, hygiene promotion, expansion of WASH services in communal centres, and the ensuring of availability of menstrual hygiene management for women and adolescent girls.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, particularly the most marginalized, can equitably access essential services that meet minimum quality standards.
ou.name: Output 1.4: Inclusive, equitable, shock responsive national safety net systems are established and operational providing support to and strengthen the resilience of the most vulnerable and marginalized people in Afghanistan.
ou.description:
In the absence of a national social protection system, the UN, with its partners, will coordinate to provide scalable and shock-responsive safety nets that complement humanitarian assistance and build the resilience of the most vulnerable. This will include gender-, age-, and disability-responsive cash or in-kind safety nets beyond 12 months, such as maternal child cash grants, cash for basic needs, protection-related support, school feeding (covered under educational support above), and take-home rations, especially for the most vulnerable groups such as female-headed households, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, among others.

Gender-responsive cash-for-work initiatives will prioritize the construction and rehabilitation of community assets that enhance community resilience by supporting livelihoods, improving access to essential services and markets, and reducing vulnerability to disasters and shocks (e.g., tertiary roads, irrigation systems, disaster risk prevention infrastructure, afforestation areas). In coordination with related activities undertaken under Strategic Priority 2, cash-for-training initiatives will build the skills of the most vulnerable based on local labour market demand to enhance employability, livelihoods, and longer-term financial stability. The UN will also work with NGOs and donor partners to develop an interim strategy to enhance coherence in approaches and funding within the sector.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, particularly the most marginalized, can equitably access essential services that meet minimum quality standards.
ou.name: Output 1.5: Relevant providers and stakeholders have strengthened capacities to increase access to and improve the provision of preventive, mitigating, and responsive protection services — including on child protection, gender-based violence, sexual exploitation and abuse, and explosive hazards — to the most vulnerable at family and community levels.
ou.description: The UN will work closely with protection partners, civil society, NGOs, employers’ and workers’ organizations, and other stakeholders to enhance their capacities and find entry points that are safe to deliver mental health and psychosocial support services — including psychosocial first aid — scale up comprehensive, quality, and survivors-centred gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response services, including initiatives to address harmful socio-cultural norms that perpetuate GBV, and risk mitigation and response services, including for domestic violence, child labour, marriage, recruitment, and sexual exploitation and abuse — such as bacha bazi20 — and other harmful practices. Provision of individualized support will be improved through the strengthening of service delivery, case management services, mapping of referral systems for women and girl survivors of violence and people with specialized needs, supporting legal identity systems (including for registration of births), and facilitating access to housing, land, and property. Community structures will be empowered with knowledge and skills and through dialogue and engagement to ensure local buy-in and ownership of protection services. Additional safe spaces will be created to ensure women facing restrictions continue to participate in community life and access essential services. Youth-friendly spaces, centres, and services will also be supported. Humanitarian mine action will mitigate the impact of explosive ordnance on civilians and enable the delivery of essential services. Direct advocacy and engagement will be undertaken with the de facto authorities on key protection concerns, particularly those related to women and children.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, notably women and vulnerable groups, will benefit from an increasingly inclusive economy, with greater equality of economic opportunities, jobs, more resilient livelihoods, strengthened food value chains, and improved natural resources management.
ou.name: Output 2.1: Economic and financial institutions and stakeholders have improved capacities to contribute to economic stabilization and pro-poor, private-sector-led economic recovery.
ou.description:
The UN and other international agencies will generate evidence-based scenario simulations using economic modelling tools to provide visibility on the future trajectories of the Afghan economy to inform economic recovery-related programmatic recommendations and contribute to more credible macroeconomic management policies that support price stability and inclusive economic growth.

Technical assistance will also be provided to financial sector institutions to develop industry- and client-specific financial products — including access to remittances and payment systems, promote learning and exchange of best practices in financing, and re-establish correspondent banking relationships with foreign banks that will foster international trade and transit.

Where appropriate, the UN and its partners will examine opportunities provided by existing/growing regional trade dynamics. Additionally, various financial guarantee schemes — such as deposit insurance and loan guarantees — will be provided with the aim of restoring trust in the banks and the market. These interventions will fuel the revitalization of banking services and the overall financial system in addition to rebuilding a pro-poor and inclusive microfinance industry.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, notably women and vulnerable groups, will benefit from an increasingly inclusive economy, with greater equality of economic opportunities, jobs, more resilient livelihoods, strengthened food value chains, and improved natural resources management.
ou.name: Output 2.2: Private sector enterprises, particularly MSMEs, have improved access to finance, asset support and business development services, and increased business opportunities that stimulate growth and decent job creation.
ou.description:
The UN and its partners will support start-ups, MSMEs, agribusinesses, and the capacity development of business services providers, including employers’ and workers’ organizations, and business development mentors to facilitate private-sector-led growth and decent job creation. Women-owned enterprises, women-led organizations, and women-focused organizations will be key beneficiaries and partners. In coordination with TVET initiatives under Strategic Priority 1, the UN will support the development of vocational skills, entrepreneurship, and life skills that match market needs and demands and enhances the livelihoods, particularly of women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized groups, as well as their participation in the labour force.

The empirical findings from these assessments will inform efforts on the development of existing market infrastructure and creation of new infrastructure and opportunities for MSMEs to enhance productivity, build on pre-existing resilience, and increase the adoption of technologies to improve productivity and standards across value chains. With its partners, the UN will also focus on increasing business opportunities, availability of market information, linkages with producers, access to financial and energy services, and cost reduction measures, particularly in targeted population centres where economic activities are concentrated and where MSMEs are typically clustered in accordance with their specific value chains. The UN will work to promote women’s participation in the economy by addressing barriers restricting their engagement, supporting women-led enterprises, and providing technical support to women entrepreneurs. The intended interventions will also promote international labour standards, including occupational safety and health and elimination of child labour and forced labour, in target MSMEs.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan, notably women and vulnerable groups, will benefit from an increasingly inclusive economy, with greater equality of economic opportunities, jobs, more resilient livelihoods, strengthened food value chains, and improved natural resources management.
ou.name: Output 2.3: Rural communities can better and sustainably manage natural resources, increase agricultural productivity and value addition, manage and reduce disaster risks, and enhance biodiversity, contributing to increased resilience, food security and nutrition, decent work, and sustainable livelihoods for all Afghans.
ou.description:
Interventions supporting rural livelihoods in an increasingly water-stressed environment will be undertaken that build the capacities of communities on the sustainable management and use of natural resources and ecosystem restoration in a conflict-sensitive manner and create opportunities to address gender inequalities. Water resource governance and management will be resourced to ensure improved access by all to clean water for human consumption (in coordination with WASH-related activities under Priority 1), equitable and stable storage and supply for agricultural production, and sustainable utilization of water resources at both community and watershed levels. Support will also promote knowledge transfer and sustainable solutions on extension services.

Geographically-tailored interventions will seek to increase food production, reduce food loss, mitigate the impact of natural disasters, improve productivity of vulnerable farmers and herders, and strengthen food value chains capable of improving food security and nutrition for the most vulnerable, including through improved knowledge and skills — such as through extension and farmer field schools — productive inputs and assets, and access to energy, credit, and markets. These initiatives will seek to create opportunities for women to improve access to access land, productive assets, credit, and markets and to engage women, who are most affected by food insecurity, in the food value chain. Construction or rehabilitation of small-scale community infrastructure using employment-intensive and climate-resilient approaches — including roads, bridges, water harvesting and storage structures, irrigation structures, water and soil conservation and clean energy technologies, flood mitigation infrastructure, reservoirs, cold storage, mini-power grids, and processing centres, and preservation of cultural heritage — will be supported in consultation with communities to strengthen community resilience to natural shocks, create jobs, and stimulate economic recovery and community development. The UN and its partners will also consider if and how infrastructure projects left incomplete after August 2021 could be finalized. Ownership, maintenance, and sustainability of facilities will be carefully considered on a case-by-case basis. Disaster risk reduction and early warning systems will be promoted to mitigate the impacts of drought, floods, and other natural disasters on agricultural production and livelihoods. Finally, in response to the opium poppy ban and its consequences, support will be provided for a swift transition of poppy-reliant communities to sustainable and licit livelihoods.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan can participate in an increasingly socially cohesive, gender-equal, and inclusive society, where the rule of law and human rights are progressively upheld, and more people can participate in governance and decision-making.
ou.name: Output 3.1: Formal and informal governance mechanisms, community-based institutions, and decision-making platforms are more inclusive, responsive, accountable, and better able to contribute to social cohesion and reconciliation.
ou.description:
The UN will support relevant policy platforms to ensure that all Afghans, particularly women and other groups excluded from national and local decision-making processes, can influence policymaking impacting Afghanistan’s future. Enhanced coordination across platforms — particularly those bringing Afghan women, youth, and other excluded groups together and ensuring that various forums inform international decision-making — will be key.

Interventions will advocate advancing inclusive participation in decision-making processes through formal institutions and informal platforms at all levels, to enhance responsive, inclusive, transparent, and accountable governance. This will include strengthening the capacity of Community Development Councils, among others, to enable transparent and gender-equitable decision-making and delivery of aid and promotion of rights.

The UN will promote and support the establishment of local, inclusive mechanisms to build social cohesion within and across communities, including within displaced communities, and address drivers of conflict and social inequalities. Social cohesion will integrate gender across all areas of work to ensure that all activities and interventions create spaces for women to participate and for gender equality concerns to be addressed.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan can participate in an increasingly socially cohesive, gender-equal, and inclusive society, where the rule of law and human rights are progressively upheld, and more people can participate in governance and decision-making.
ou.name: Output 3.2: Justice institutions, including customary and traditional community systems, are better able to provide accessible, effective, equitable, inclusive, transparent, and timely services, and these services are increasingly provided in line with international norms and standards, benefiting all communities, especially vulnerable groups such as women, children, and minorities.
ou.description:
The UN will lead, support, and amplify coordinated advocacy initiatives that promote adherence to the rule of law and access to justice in Afghanistan, including by advocating for processes that clarify legal and constitutional frameworks that uphold international norms and standards, especially human rights. iven the absence of women’s access to ustice across the country, special emphasis will be placed on addressing severe gender gaps.

Support will create legal awareness among communities, focusing on women and girls, and sensitizing them on their human rights and access to justice mechanisms. Special focus will be placed on supporting gender and age-sensitive access to and meaningful participation in the justice system and reducing the impact of harmful and discriminatory practices against women, children, persons with disabilities, and minority groups.

Flexible, long-term funding will be provided to civil society – especially women-led civil society – in strengthening bottom-up approaches to social cohesion and inclusion, access to justice, protection, and the promotion of human rights while ensuring transparency and accountability. The UN will further advocate for legislation, institutional frameworks, and policies that comply with the United Nations Convention Against Corruption.

ou.parentName: By the end of 2027, more people in Afghanistan can participate in an increasingly socially cohesive, gender-equal, and inclusive society, where the rule of law and human rights are progressively upheld, and more people can participate in governance and decision-making.
ou.name: Output 3.3: Communities, civil society organizations, vulnerable groups, women, and other relevant stakeholders are more aware of and better able to promote and protect their human rights, aligned with international norms and standards, and mitigate threats to their safety and wellbeing.
ou.description:
The UN will advocate for the promotion and protection of human rights and the alignment of Afghanistan’s normative and legal frameworks with international human rights instruments. Advocacy and behaviour change interventions will be pursued to address policies, structures, and harmful socio-cultural norms that perpetuate underlying drivers of social inequalities and conflict. Given the systematic erasure of the rights of women and girls across all spheres of life, the UN will work to restore women’s rights and find practical ways to improve the daily lives of women and girls, including their labour rights. Through both technical and financial means, the UNCT will support grassroots organisations present in the country to preserve civic space.

Sex and age disaggregated data and reports will be produced to monitor excluded and at-risk groups, human rights threats, and violations to inform the UN response.

Awareness of human rights will be increased and capacities built, particularly of marginalized and at-risk groups, to identify and prevent rights violations (including those that have been normalized due to harmful socio-cultural norms) and effectively advocate for their rights. Flexible, long-term funding will be provided to community structures, civil society — especially women-led civil society — NGOs, human rights defenders, and labour-related organizations to advance human rights, labour rights, and gender equality. Freedom of association, access to information, ending impunity of violence against journalists, peaceful assembly, opinion, and expression will also be promoted, including through support for a free and independent media.

sp.name: Inclusive Social and Human Development
sp.description:
Strategic Priority 1: Inclusive Social and Human Development
The UN will work with partners to strengthen health, education, social protection, and GBV response systems to ensure equitable access and inclusion for all, especially vulnerable groups. Key focus areas include:

Health and Well-Being: Advancing primary health care, hospital reforms, universal health coverage, digital health systems, and healthy ageing, while addressing social determinants and health security under a One Health approach.
Inclusive, Quality Education: Expanding access to pre-school and quality education, optimizing school networks, promoting inclusive curricula, teacher training, and healthier learning environments, with targeted support for Roma, children with disabilities, and displaced children.
Responsive Social Protection: Enhancing policy frameworks, case management, and service delivery for vulnerable populations, introducing the European Child Guarantee, and improving coordination among social protection actors.
Gender-Based Violence Response: Strengthening institutional and multisectoral responses, survivor-centred services, and public awareness campaigns, aligned with the Istanbul Convention.

All interventions will uphold the principle of Leave No One Behind, engaging civil society, private sector, and government institutions to ensure inclusive, gender-responsive, and rights-based approaches.

sp.name: Sustainable Economy and Decent Work
sp.description:
Strategic Priority 2: Sustainable Economy and Decent Work
The UN will support North Macedonia in fostering an enabling economic environment, creating decent work opportunities, and promoting inclusive growth. Key focus areas include:

Economic Enabling Environment: Strengthening labour market institutions, addressing labour shortages, promoting labour mobility, integrating vulnerable groups, and supporting green transition and agri-food system resilience. Efforts also include enhancing trade and transport connectivity, cultural and creative industries, and innovation aligned with EU standards.
Vocational Training and Skills Development: Scaling up VET and lifelong learning, introducing green and digital curricula, and improving employability for women, youth, persons with disabilities, and rural populations. Special emphasis on care sector skills and part-time employment opportunities.
Women’s Economic Empowerment: Advancing gender equality in the labour market through policy reforms, research on pay gaps and unpaid care work, promoting family-friendly policies, and addressing barriers in STEM and ICT fields.

All interventions prioritize Leave No One Behind, ensuring vulnerable groups have equitable access to skills development and employment. Partnerships will include government institutions, private sector, social partners, civil society, and international development actors.

sp.name: Resilient and Green Society and Ecosystems
sp.description:
Strategic Priority 3: Resilient and Green Society and Ecosystems
The UN will support North Macedonia in advancing climate action, disaster resilience, pollution reduction, and biodiversity conservation to build a greener and more sustainable future. Key focus areas include:

Climate Action and Disaster Resilience: Developing gender-responsive climate policies, strengthening institutional capacities, accessing climate finance, and promoting clean energy solutions. Efforts include adaptation in agriculture, forestry, water, and health systems, and reforming disaster risk management in line with the Sendai Framework.
Pollution Action: Reducing air pollution from transport, industry, and waste burning; improving solid and hazardous waste management; promoting circular economy practices; and supporting compliance with Multilateral Environmental Agreements.
Environmental Protection and Natural Resource Management: Enhancing biodiversity conservation, managing protected areas and UNESCO sites, fostering transboundary cooperation, and integrating nature-based solutions into economic sectors. Focus also includes sustainable water and land management and citizen science initiatives.

All interventions prioritize Leave No One Behind, ensuring vulnerable groups are engaged and protected from climate and environmental risks. Partnerships will span government institutions, civil society, private sector, and international financing mechanisms to accelerate green transformation.

sp.name: Rule of Law and Good Governance
sp.description:
Strategic Priority 4: Rule of Law and Good Governance
The UN will support North Macedonia in strengthening governance, justice, and inclusive participation to advance EU accession and uphold human rights. Key focus areas include:

Good Governance: Enhancing institutional capacities, legislative alignment, decentralization reforms, and public service delivery. Support includes fiscal efficiency, gender-responsive budgeting, digital transformation, cybersecurity, and improved statistical systems for evidence-based policymaking.
Justice, Rule of Law, and Human Rights: Strengthening justice institutions, access to legal aid, anti-corruption measures, and compliance with international human rights standards. Efforts also address organized crime, trafficking, money laundering, and terrorism financing.
Women, Youth, and Civil Society Participation: Promoting inclusive decision-making and social cohesion through capacity building for women, youth, and civil society organizations, fostering accountability, and advancing gender-responsive governance.

All interventions prioritize Leave No One Behind, ensuring vulnerable groups’ rights and participation are integrated into governance and justice reforms. Partnerships will include government institutions, civil society, private sector, and international actors, including the EU and OSCE.
